βα.def: βᾶ (shortd. form of voc. Βασιλεῦ) king! Aesch.

βαβαι.def: βαβαί Lat. papae! exclamation of surprise, bless me! Eur., Ar.

βαβυκα.def: βαβύκα (Lacon. for γέφυρα, Arist. ap. Plut.)

βαδην.def: βάδην (βαίνω) I. step by step, Lat. pedetentim, Il.; in marching step, Hdt.; β. ταχύ at quick step, Xen. 2. gradually, more and more, Ar. II. walking, marching, opp. to riding, driving, sailing, Aesch.

βαδιζω.def: βαδίζω (βάδος, βαίνω) 1. to go slowly, to walk, Lat. ambulare, Hhymn., Xen.: to go, march, of horsemen, id.: to go by land, Dem.:—c. acc. cogn., βάδον, ὁδὸν β. Ar., Xen. 2. generally, ἐπ’ οἰκίας βαδ. to enter houses, Dem.: to proceed (in argument), id.:—of things, αἱ τιμαὶ ἐπ’ ἔλαττον ἐβάδιζον prices were getting lower, id.

βαδισισ.def: βάδισις (from βαδίζω) a walking, going, Ar.; of hares, Xen.

βαδισμα.def: βάδισμα (from βαδίζω) walk, gait, Xen., Dem.

βαδιστεοσ.def: βαδιστέος (verb. adj. of βαδίζω) one must walk or go, Soph.:—so pl. βαδιστέα, Ar.

βαδιστησ.def: βαδιστής (βαδίζω) a goer, ταχὺς βαδ. a quick runner, Eur.

βαδοσ.def: βάδος (βαίνω) a walk, βάδον βαδίζειν Ar.

βαζω.def: βάζω (chiefly in pres. and imperf.) to speak, say, Hom.; βάζειν τί τινα to say somewhat to a man, Il.; also, τί τινί Aesch.; c. dat. modi, χαλεποῖς βάζειν ἐπέεσσι to address with sharp words, Hes.:—Pass., ἔπος βέβακται a word has been spoken, Od.

βαθμοσ.def: βαθμός (βαίνω) a step: metaph. a step, degree, NTest.

βαθοσ.def: βάθος (βαθύς) 1. depth or height, acc. as measured up or down, Lat. altitudo, Ταρτάρου βάθη Aesch.; αἰθέρος βάθος Eur.: in military sense, the depth of a line of battle, Thuc., Xen.:— β. τριχῶν depth, i. e. thickness or length, of hair, Hdt.:—in NTest., τὸ βάθος the deep water. 2. metaph., κακῶν βάθος Aesch.; πλούτου βάθος Soph.

βαθρον.def: βάθρον (shortd. from βατήριον) (βαίνω) that on which anything stands: 1. a base, pedestal, Hdt., Aesch. 2. a stage or scaffold, Hdt. 3. generally solid ground, Σαλαμῖνος β. Soph.; ὦ πατρῶιον ἑστίας βάθρον i. e. house of my father, id.:—in pl. foundations, Eur.; ἐν βάθροις εἶναι to stand firm, id. 4. a step, Soph.; the round of a ladder, Eur. 5. a bench, seat, Soph., Dem. 6. metaph., κινδύνου βάθρα the verge of danger, Eur.

βαθυγαιοσ.def: βαθύγαιος (γαῖα) with deep soil, productive, Hdt.

βαθυγηρωσ.def: βαθύγηρως (γῆρας) in great old age, decrepit, Anth.

βαθυζωνοσ.def: βαθύζωνος (ζώνη) deep-girded, i. e. girded not close under the breast, but over the hips, so that the gown fell over the girdle in folds (cf. βαθύκολπος), Hom.

βαθυθριξ.def: βαθύθριξ of sheep, with thick wool, Hhymn.

βαθυκητησ.def: βαθυκήτης (κῆτος II) deep yawning, of the sea, Theogn.

βαθυκολποσ.gloss: with dress falling in deep folds
βαθυκολποσ.def: βαθύκολπος I. with dress falling in deep folds (cf. βαθύζωνος), of Trojan women, Il. II. with deep, full breasts, deep-bosomed, Aesch.; of the earth, Pind.: cf. βαθύστερνος.

βαθυκρημνοσ.def: βαθύκρημνος with high cliffs, ἅλς Pind.; β. ἀκταί deep and rugged headlands, id.

βαθυκτεανοσ.def: βαθυκτέανος (κτέανον) with great possessions, plenteous, Anth.

βαθυλειμοσ.def: βαθύλειμος (λειμών) with deep, rich meadows, Il.

βαθυληιοσ.def: βαθυλήιος (λήϊον) with deep crop, very fruitful, Il.

βαθυνω.def: βαθύνω (βαθύς) 1. to deepen, hollow out, of a torrent, Il.: to dig deep, NTest. 2. as military term, to deepen, τὴν φάλαγγα Xen.

βαθυπολεμοσ.def: βαθυπόλεμος plunged deep in war, Pind.

βαθυσ.def: βαθύς I. deep or high, acc. to one's position, like Lat. altus, Hom., etc.; βαθέης αὐλῆς from high-fenced court, Il.; ἠιόνος προπάροιθε βαθείης the deep, i. e. wide, shore, id.; in Prose, of a line of battle, Xen. 2. deep or thick in substance, of a mist, Hom.; of ploughed land, opp. to stony ground, Il., Eur.:— deep, thick, of woods, corn, clouds, Il., Hdt., etc.; of hair, Xen. 3. violent, of a storm, Il. 4. generally, large, copious, abundant, κλέος, κλῆρος Pind.; βαθεῖα τέρψις Soph.; βαθὺς ἀνήρ a rich man, Xen.; β. ὕπνος deep sleep, Theocr. 5. of the mind, deep, Il., Aesch.; βαθύτερα ἤθεα Hdt. 6. of Time, far-advanced, late, βαθὺς ὄρθρος (v. ὄρθρος); βαθὺ τῆς ἡλικίας Ar.; β. γῆρας Anth. II. adv. βαθέως, Theocr.

βαθυστερνοσ.def: βαθύστερνος (στέρνον) deep-chested, λέων Pind., cf. βαθύκολπος.

βαθυστολμοσ.def: βαθύστολμος with deep, full robe, Anth.

βαθυχαιτησ.def: βαθυχαίτης (χαίτη) with deep, thick hair, Hes.

βαινω.def: βαίνω (Root ΒΑ) A. in most forms, I. intr. to walk, step, properly of motion on foot, ποσσὶ or ποσὶ βαίνειν Hom., etc.; c. inf. in Hom., βῆ ἰέναι, βῆ ἰέμεν set out to go, went his way, Il.; βῆ θέειν started to run, id.; βῆ δ’ ἐλάαν, id., etc.:—c. acc. loci, Soph.; and with all Preps. implying motion, as, ἐπὶ νηὸς ἔβαινεν was going on board ship, Od.; ἐφ’ ἵππων βάντες having mounted the chariot, id.; βαίνειν δι’ αἵματος to wade through blood, Eur., etc. 2. in perf. to stand or be in a place, χῶρος ἐν ὧι βεβήκαμεν Soph.; often αλμοστ͂ εἰμί (sum), εὖ βεβηκώς on a good footing, well established, prosperous, Hdt., etc.; so, οἱ ἐν τέλει βεβῶτες they who are in office, id., Soph.; cf. ξυρόν. 3. to go, go away, depart, Il., Soph.; βέβηκα euphem. for τέθνηκα, Aesch., Soph.:—of things, ἐννέα ἐνιαυτοὶ βεβάασι nine years have come and gone, Il. 4. to come, τίπτε βέβηκας; id.: to arrive, Soph. 5. to go on, advance, ἐς τόδε τόλμης, ἐς τοσοῦτον ἐλπίδων id. II. c. acc. to mount, Hom. only in aor1 mid., βήσασθαι δίφρον:— Pass., ἵπποι βαινόμεναι brood mares, Hdt. 2. χρέος ἔβα με debts came on me, Ar. 3. in Poets, with acc. of the instrument of motion, which is simply pleonastic, βαίνειν πόδα to advance the foot, step on, Eur., etc. B. Causal, in fut. βήσω, aor1 ἔβησα:— to make to go, βῆσεν ἀφ’ ἵππον, ἐξ ἵππων βῆσε brought them down from the chariot, Il. The pres. in this sense is βιβάζω.

βαιοσ.def: βαιός little, small, scanty, and of number, few, Pind., Aesch., Soph.; ἐχώρει βαιός he was going with scanty escort, i. e. alone, id.: of condition, low, mean, humble, id.: of time, short, Solon, Soph.:— neut. βαιόν, as adv. a little, id.; so pl. βαιά, Ar. Cf. ἠβαιός.

βαιτη.def: βαίτη (deriv. uncertain) a shepherd's or peasant's coat of skins, Hdt., Theocr.

βακελασ.gloss: an eunuch in the service of Cybele
βακελασ.def: βακέλας an eunuch in the service of Cybele, Anth., Luc.

βακιζω.def: Βακίζω (from Βακίς) to prophesy like Bacis, Ar.

βακισ.def: Βακίς an old Boeotian prophet, Hdt.

βακλον.def: βάκλον Lat. baculum, a stick, Aesop.

βακτηρια.def: βακτηρία (= βάκτρον,) a staff, cane, Ar., Thuc.: borne as a badge of office by the δικασταί, Dem.

βακτρευμα.def: βάκτρευμα (from βακτρεύω) a staff, βακτρεύματα ποδός support lent to one's foot, Eur.

βακτρευω.def: βακτρεύω to lean on a staff.

βακτρον.def: βάκτρον (βιβάζω) Lat. baculus, a staff, stick, cudgel, Aesch., Eur.

βακτροπροσαιτησ.gloss: going about begging with a staff
βακτροπροσαιτησ.def: βακτροπροσαίτης going about begging with a staff, of a Cynic, Anth.

βακυλον.def: βάκυλον = βάκλον: pl. = Lat. fasces, Plut.

βακχαω.gloss: to be in Bacchic frenzy, to rave
βακχαω.def: Βακχάω (Βάκχη) to be in Bacchic frenzy, to rave, Aesch.

βακχεβακχον.def: Βακχέβακχον βακχέβακχον ἆισαι, to sing the song Βάκχε Βάκχε! Ar.

βακχεια.gloss: the feast of Bacchus, Bacchic frenzy, revelry
βακχεια.def: Βακχεία the feast of Bacchus, Bacchic frenzy, revelry, Aesch., Eur.: generally, frenzy, Plat.:—in pl. Bacchic orgies, Eur.

βακχειον.def: Βακχεῖον I. the temple of Bacchus, Ar. II. Bacchic revelry, Eur.:—in pl. Bacchic orgies, Ar.; also Βάκχια, Eur.

βακχειοσ.def: Βάκχειος (Βάκχος) I. Bacchic, of or belonging to Bacchus and his rites, Eur., Xen.; frenzied, frenzy-stricken, Hdt., Soph.; τὸν B. ἄνακτα, of Aeschylus, Ar. II. as Subst., Βάκχιος, ὁ, Βάκχος, Soph., Eur. 2. = οἶνος, id. 3. Βάκχειος (sc. πούς), a foot of three syllables, ˘ ˘ ¯ opp. to antibacchius.

βακχευμα.def: Βάκχευμα (Βακχεύω) in pl. Bacchic revelries, Eur., Plut.

βακχευτησ.def: Βακχευτής a Bacchanal: as adj. Bacchanalian, Anth.

βακχευτικοσ.def: Βακχευτικός (from Βακχευτής) disposed to Bacchic revels, Arist.

βακχευω.gloss: to keep the feast of Bacchus, celebrate his mysteries
βακχευω.def: Βακχεύω (Βάκχος) I. to keep the feast of Bacchus, celebrate his mysteries, Hdt. 2. to speak or act like one frantic, Lat. bacchari, Soph., Eur. II. Causal, to inspire with frenzy, id.:—Pass., id.

βακχη.def: Βάκχη a Bacchante, Aesch., Soph., etc.:—generally, Βάκχη Ἅιδου frantic handmaid of Hades, Eur.; β. νεκύων id.

βακχοσ.def: Βάκχος (The Root seems to be ϜΑΧ, so that Βάκχος represents ϝάκχος; and Ἴακχος is for ϝίϝακχος; prob. from ἰάχω, ϝιϝάχω, to shout) I. Bacchus, a later name of Dionysus, Soph., etc.: called Διόνυσος Βάκχειος and ὁ Βάκχειος in Hdt. II. as appellat. wine, Eur., etc. III. a Bacchanal, any one inspired, frantic, id., Plat.

βαλαναγρα.def: βαλανάγρα (βάλανος II) a key or hook for pulling out the doorpin, Hdt., Xen.

βαλανειον.def: βαλανεῖον (from βαλανεύς) Lat. balineum, balneum, a bath or bathing-room, Ar.; in pl., id.

βαλανευσ.def: βαλανεύς (deriv. uncertain) a bath-man, Lat. balneator.

βαλανευω.def: βαλανεύω (βαλανεύς) to wait upon a person at the bath, β. ἑαυτῶι to be one's own bath-man, Ar.

βαλανιζω.def: βαλανίζω βαλανίζω δρῦν, to shake acorns from the oak: as a proverb. answer to beggars, ἄλλην δρῦν βαλάνιζε Anth.

βαλανισσα.def: βαλάνισσα (fem. of βαλανεύς) a bathing-woman, Anth.

βαλανοδοκη.gloss: the socket in a door-post to receive the
βαλανοδοκη.def: βαλανοδόκη (δέχομαι) the socket in a door-post to receive the βάλανος (II).

βαλανοσ.def: βάλανος (deriv. uncertain) I. an acorn, Lat. glans, the fruit of the φηγός, given to swine, Od.:— any similar fruit, the date, Hdt., Xen. II. from similarity of shape, an iron peg, a bolt-pin, Lat. pessulus, passed through the wooden bar (μοχλός) into the door-post, so that the bar could not be removed till the pin was taken out with a hook (βαλανάγρα), Ar., Thuc.

βαλανοω.def: βαλανόω (from βάλανος) to fasten with a bolt-pin (βάλανος II), βεβαλάνωκε τὴν θύραν Ar.:—Pass., βεβαλανωμένος, η, ον, shut close, secured, id.

βαλβισ.gloss: the rope drawn across the race-course
βαλβισ.def: βαλβίς (deriv. uncertain) I. properly, the rope drawn across the race-course: mostly in pl., Lat. carceres, the posts marking the line whence the racers started, and to which they returned, Ar.:—then, any starting point, Eur., Ar.; metaph., πρὸς βαλβῖδα βίου Eur. II. also any point to be gained, as the battlements (by one scaling a wall), Soph.

βαλιοσ.def: Βάλιος parox. Βαλίος, one of the horses of Achilles, dapple, Il.

βαλλαντιον.def: βαλλάντιον a bag, pouch, purse, Simon., Ar.

βαλλαντιοτομεω.def: βαλλαντιοτομέω (from βαλλαντιοτόμος) to cut purses, Plat., Xen.

βαλλην.def: βαλλήν (Prob. from Baal, Bel.) a king, Aesch.

βαλληναδε.def: βαλληνάδε βαλληνάδε βλέπειν, a pun between βάλλω and the Attic deme Παλλήνη, Ar.

βαλλω.def: βάλλω (Root ΒΑΛ) A. Act. to throw: I. with acc. of person or thing aimed at, to throw so as to hit, to hit one with a missile, opp. to striking (τύπτω, οὐτάω), βλήμενος ἠὲ τυπείς Il.; c. dupl. acc. pers. et partis, μιν βάλε μηρὸν ὀϊστῶι id.: c. acc. cogn. added, ἕλκος, τό μιν βάλε the wound which he gave him, id.:—also, βάλε κατ’ ἀσπίδα smote upon it, id. 2. of things, ἡνίοχον ῥαθάμιγγες ἔβαλλον id.; of the Sun, ἀκτῖσιν ἔβαλλεν [χθόνα] Od.: to strike the senses, of sound, κτύπος οὔατα βάλλει Il. 3. metaph., β. τινὰ κακοῖς to smite with reproaches, Soph., etc.; φθόνος βάλλει τινά Aesch. II. with acc. of the weapon thrown, to throw, cast, hurl, βαλὼν βέλος Il; ἐν νηυσὶν πῦρ βάλλειν id.:—with dat. of the weapon, to throw or shoot with a thing, χερμαδίοισι id.; βέλεσι β. τινα Hom.; β. ἐπί τινα to throw at one, Thuc.; ἐπὶ σκοπόν or σκοποῦ Xen. 2. generally of anything thrown, εἰς ἅλα λύματ’ ἔβαλλον Il., etc.:—of persons, β. τινὰ ἐν κονίηισιν, ἐν δαπέδωι Hom., etc.; metaph., ἐς κακὸν β. τινά Od.; β. τινὰ ἐς φόβον Eur.; also, ἐν αἰτίαι or αἰτία β. τινά Soph. 3. to let fall, ἑτέρωσε κάρη βάλεν Il.; β. ἀπὸ δάκρυ παρειῶν Od. 4. of the eyes, ἑτέρωσε βάλ’ ὄμματα cast them the other way, id., etc. 5. in a loose sense, to throw, to put, place, ἐν στήθεσσι μένος βάλε Il.; ὅπως φιλότητα μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισι βάλωμεν may put frienship between them, id.; β. τί τινι ἐν θυμῶι Od.; ἐς θυμὸν β. to lay to heart, Soph. 6. to put round, ἀμφ’ ὀχέεσσι βάλε κύκλα Il.; and of clothes or arms, ἀμφὶ δ’ Ἀθήνη ὤμοις βάλ’ αἰγίδα id. 7. βαλών is sometimes added, like λαβών or ἔχων, at the end of a sentence, almost as an expletive, with, Soph. III. intr., ποταμὸς εἰς ἅλα βάλλων falling, Il.; ἐν πέδωι βαλῶ (sc. ἐμαυτήν) Aesch. 2. so in familiar language, βάλλ’ ἐς κόρακας away with you! be hanged! Lat. pasce corvos! abi in malam rem! Ar. B. Mid. to put for oneself, ἐνὶ θυμῶι βάλλευ lay it to heart, Od.; ἐς θυμὸν βάλλεσθαί τι Hdt.; ἐφ’ ἑωυτοῦ βαλόμενος on one's own judgment, of oneself, id. 2. τόξα or ξίφος ἀμφ’ ὤμοις βάλλεσθαι to throw about one's shoulder, Il. 3. ἐς γαστέρα βάλλεσθαι, of a woman, to conceive, Hdt. 4. to lay the foundations of, begin to form, οἰκοδομίαν, στρατόπεδον, Plat., etc.; β. ἄγκυραν to cast anchor, Hdt. II. rarely, χρόα βάλλεσθαι λουτροῖς to dash one's flesh with water, bathe, Hhymn.

βαμβαινω.def: βαμβαίνω (Formed from the sound.) (only in pres.) to chatter with the teeth, Il.: to stammer, Bion.

βαμμα.gloss: that in which a thing is dipped, dye
βαμμα.def: βάμμα (βάπτω) that in which a thing is dipped, dye, Plat., v. βάπτω I. 3.

βαναυσια.gloss: handicraft, the practice of a mere mechanical art
βαναυσια.def: βαναυσία (from βάναυσος) handicraft, the practice of a mere mechanical art, Hdt.

βαναυσικοσ.def: βαναυσικός (from βάναυσος) of or for mechanics: τέχνη β. a mere mechanical art, Lat. ars sellularia, Xen.

βαναυσοσ.def: βάναυσος (deriv. uncertain) I. mechanical, and as Subst. a mechanic, Arist. II. τέχνη βάναυσος a mere mechanical art, a base, ignoble art, Soph., Plat.

βαξισ.def: βάξις (βάζω) 1. a saying, esp. an oracular saying, like φήμη, Aesch., Soph. 2. a report, rumour, Theogn., Soph., Eur.; ἁλώσιμος β. tidings of the capture, Aesch.

βαπτιζω.def: βαπτίζω 1. to dip in or under water; metaph., βεβαπτισμένοι soaked in wine, Plat.; ὀφλήμασι βεβ. over head and ears in debt, Plut. 2. to baptize, τινά NTest.:—Pass., βαπτίζεσθαι εἰς μετάνοιαν, εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν id.:—Mid. to get oneself baptized, id.

βαπτισμοσ.def: βαπτισμός a dipping in water, ablution, NTest.

βαπτιστησ.def: βαπτιστής one that dips: a baptizer, ὁ B. the baptist, NTest.

βαπτοσ.def: βαπτός (from βάπτω) I. dipped, dyed, bright-coloured, Ar. 2. for dyeing, χρώματα Plat. II. of water, drawn by dipping vessels (cf. βάπτω I. 3), Eur.

βαπτω.def: βάπτω (Root ΒΑΦ) I. trans. to dip in water, Lat. immergere, Od., Plat.:—of slaughter, ἐν σφαγαῖσι βάψασα ξίφος Aesch.; ἔβαψας ἔγχος Soph.; φάσγανον εἴσω σαρκὸς ἔβαψεν Eur. 2. to dip in poison, ἰούς, χιτῶνα Soph. 3. to dip in dye, to dye, Hdt., Aesch.:—Comic, βάπτειν τινὰ βάμμα Σαρδιανικόν to dye one in the [red] dye of Sardis, i. e. give him a bloody coxcomb, Ar. 4. to draw water by dipping a vessel, Theocr.; βάψασα ἁλός (sc. τὸ τεῦχος) having dipped it so as to draw water from the sea, Eur. II. intr., ναῦς ἔβαψεν the ship dipped, sank, id.

βαραθρον.def: βάραθρον (deriv. uncertain) 1. a gulf, pit:— at Athens a cleft behind the Acropolis, into which criminals were thrown, Hdt., Ar. 2. metaph. ruin, perdition, Dem.

βαρβαριζω.gloss: to behave like a barbarian, speak like one
βαρβαριζω.def: βαρβαρίζω (βάρβαρος) I. to behave like a barbarian, speak like one, Hdt.: to speak broken Greek, speak gibberish, Plat. II. to hold with the barbarians, i. e. the Persians, Xen.

βαρβαρικοσ.def: βαρβαρικός barbaric, foreign, like a foreigner, opp. to Ἑλληνικός, Simon.; τὸ βαρβαρικόν, οἱ βάρβαροι, Thuc.; esp. of the Persians, Xen.:—adv., βαρβαρικῶς καὶ Ἑλληνικῶς i. e. both in Persian and Greek, id.

βαρβαροομαι.def: βαρβαρόομαι Pass. to become barbarous, Eur.; βεβαρβαρωμένος of barbarous or outlandish sound, Soph.

βαρβαροσ.def: βάρβαρος (deriv. uncertain) I. barbarous, i. e. not Greek, foreign, known to Hom., as appears from the word βαρβαρόφωνος in Il.:—as Subst. βάρβαροι, οἱ, originally all that were not Greeks, specially the Medes and Persians, Hdt., attic: so the Hebrews called the rest of mankind Gentiles. From the Augustan age however the name was given by the Romans to all tribes which had no Greek or Roman accomplishments. II. after the Persian war the word took the sense of outlandish, ἀμαθὴς καὶ βάρβαρος Ar.; βαρβαρώτατος id., Thuc.

βαρβαροφωνοσ.def: βαρβαρόφωνος (φωνή) speaking a foreign tongue, Κᾶρες Il.

βαρβιτοσ.gloss: a musical instrument of many strings
βαρβιτοσ.def: βάρβιτος (Prob. and Oriental word.) a musical instrument of many strings (πολύχορδος Theocr.), like the lyre, and often used for the lyre itself, Anacr., Eur., etc.

βαρδιστοσ.def: βάρδιστος (by epic metath. for βράδιστος, Sup.of βραδύς, Il.)

βαρεω.def: βαρέω (βαρύς) I. to weigh down, depress, Luc. II. intr. in epic perf. part. βεβαρηώς, weighed down, heavy, οἴνωι βεβαρηότες Od.: later in part. pass. βεβαρημένος, Theocr., Anth., etc.

βαρισ.def: βᾶρις a flat-bottomed boat, used in Egypt, Hdt., Aesch.

βαροσ.def: βάρος (βαρύς) I. weight, Hdt., etc. II. a weight, burden, load, Aesch., etc. III. metaph. a heavy weight, πημονῆς, συμφορᾶς β. Soph.; then alone for grief, misery, Aesch.; βάρος ἔχειν Arist. IV. abundance, πλούτου, ὄλβου Eur.

βαρυγυιοσ.def: βαρύγυιος (γυῖον) weighing down the limbs, wearisome, Anth.

βαρυδαιμονεω.def: βαρυδαιμονέω to be grievously unlucky, Ar.

βαρυδαιμων.gloss: pressed by a heavy fate, luckless
βαρυδαιμων.def: βαρυδαίμων pressed by a heavy fate, luckless, Eur.

βαρυδοτειρα.def: βαρυδότειρα giver of ill gifts, Aesch.

βαρυθυμεω.gloss: to be weighed down: to be heavy at heart
βαρυθυμεω.def: βαρυθυμέω (from βαρύθυμος) to be weighed down: to be heavy at heart: in Mid., Plut.

βαρυθυμοσ.def: βαρύθυμος heavy in spirit: indignant, sullen, Eur.

βαρυθω.def: βαρύθω (βαρύς) (only in pres. and imperf.) 1. to be weighed down, Il., Hes. 2. to be heavy, Anth.

βαρυμηνισ.def: βαρύμηνις heavy in wrath, exceeding wrathful, Aesch.

βαρυνω.gloss: to weigh down, oppress by weight, depress
βαρυνω.def: βαρύνω (βαρύς) 1. to weigh down, oppress by weight, depress, Hom.:—Pass., γυῖα βαρύνεται he is heavy, i. e. weary, in limb, Il.; χεῖρα βαρυνθείς disabled in hand, id.; βαρύνεταί τινι τὸ σκέλος Ar.; ὄμμα β., of one dying, Eur. 2. metaph. to oppress, weary, τοὺς δικαστάς Xen.:—Pass. to be oppressed, distressed, Lat. gravari, Aesch., Soph.

βαρυποτμοσ.def: βαρύποτμος (= βαρυδαίμων) (irreg. Sup. βαρυποτμώτατος (metri grat.) Eur.) of persons, Soph.; of sufferings, grievous, id.

βαρυπουσ.def: βαρύπους heavy at the end, Anth.

βαρυσ.def: βαρύς (poet. gen. pl. fem. βαρεῶν for βαρειῶν) I. heavy in weight, opp. to κοῦφος, Hdt., etc.: in Hom. mostly with a notion of strength and force, χεῖρα βαρεῖαν Il., etc.: also, heavy with age or suffering, γήραι, νόσωι Soph. 2. heavy to bear, grievous, Hom.; βαρὺ or βαρέα στενάχειν to sob heavily, id.:—in attic, burdensome, grievous, oppressive:— adv., βαρέως φέρειν τι to take a thing ill, Lat. graviter ferre, Hdt., etc.; βαρέως ἀκούειν to hear with disgust, Xen. 3. violent, Theocr., Plat., etc. 4. weighty, impressive, NTest. II. of persons, severe, stern, Aesch., Soph.:—also, wearisome, oppressive, Eur., Dem.: in good sense, grave, dignified, Arist. 2. of soldiers, heavy-armed, Xen. III. of impressions on the senses, 1. of sound, strong, deep, bass, Od., Aesch., Soph. 2. of smell, strong, offensive, Hdt., Soph.

βαρυστονοσ.def: βαρύστονος (στένω) I. groaning heavily, bellowing, Dem.:—adv. -νως, Aesch. II. of things, heavily lamented, grievous, Soph.

βαρυτησ.def: βαρύτης (βαρύς) I. weight, heaviness, Thuc. II. of men, importunity, disagreeableness, Dem., Plut. 2. in good sense, gravity, dignity, Arist., Plut. III. of sound, strength, depth, Plat.

βαρυτλητοσ.def: βαρύτλητος I. bearing a heavy weight, Anth. II. pass. ill to bear, id.

βαρυφρων.def: βαρύφρων (φρήν) weighty of purpose, grave-minded, Theocr.

βαρυψυχοσ.def: βαρύψυχος (ψυχή) heavy of soul, dejected, Soph.

βασανιζω.def: βασανίζω I. to rub gold upon the touch-stone (βάσανος), Plat.: hence, to try the genuineness of a thing, to put to the test, make proof of, id. II. of persons, to examine closely, cross-question, Hdt., Ar. 2. to question by applying torture, to torture, id.:—Pass. to be put to the torture, for the purpose of extorting confession, Thuc.: to be tormented by disease or storm, NTest.

βασανιστεοσ.gloss: to be put to the proof
βασανιστεοσ.def: βασανιστέος (verb. adj. from βασανίζω) I. to be put to the proof, Plat. II. βασανιστέον one must put to the torture, τινά id., Dem.

βασανιστησ.def: βασανιστής (βασανίζω) questioner, torturer, tormentor, Dem., NTest.

βασανοσ.def: βάσανος (deriv. uncertain) I. the touch-stone, Lat. lapis Lydius, a dark-coloured stone on which pure gold, when rubbed, leaves a peculiar mark, Theogn.: hence. II. generally, a test, trial whether a thing be genuine or real, Hdt., Soph. III. inquiry by torture, the "question, " torture, used to extort evidence from slaves, Oratt. 2. torture of disease, NTest.

βασιλεια.def: βασίλεια (βασιλεύς) a queen, princess, Od., Aesch.
βασιλεία (βασιλεύω) a kingdom, dominion, Hdt.: hereditary monarchy, opp. to τυραννίς, Thuc., etc.

βασιλειδιον.def: βασιλείδιον (Dim. of βασιλεύς) a petty king, Plut.

βασιλειον.def: βασίλειον (βασιλεύς) 1. a kingly dwelling, palace, Xen. mostly in pl., Hdt., etc. 2. the royal treasury, id.

βασιλειοσ.def: βασίλειος (βασιλεύς) of the king, kingly, royal, Hdt., etc.

βασιλευσ.def: βασιλεύς (deriv. uncertain) I. a king, chief, Hom.: later it was an hereditary king, opp. to τύραννος, Hdt., attic; ἄναξ β. lord king, Aesch.: c. gen., β. νεῶν id.; οἰωνῶν β., of the eagle, id.:—Hom. has a comp. βασιλεύτερος more of a king, more kingly, Sup. βασιλεύτατος most kingly. 2. of the king's son, prince, or any one sharing in the government, Od. 3. generally, a lord, master, householder, Il., Pind. II. at Athens, the second of the nine Archons was called βασιλεύς; he had charge of the public worship, and the conduct of criminal processes, Plat., etc. III. after the Persian war, the king of Persia was called βασιλεύς (without the Art.), Hdt., attic; more rarely ὁ βασιλεύς, or ὁ μέγας βας. Hdt.

βασιλευω.gloss: to be king, to rule, reign
βασιλευω.def: βασιλεύω (βασιλεύς) 1. to be king, to rule, reign, Hom., etc.; of a woman, to be queen, id.; c. gen. to be king of, Od.; also, ὄφρ’ Ἰθάκης κατὰ δῆμον βασιλεύοι id.; in aor. to have become king, Hdt.; c. dat. to be king among others, Od.:—Pass. to be governed by a king, Plat.: to submit to the king, Plut. 2. to be master of a thing, c. gen., Theocr.

βασιληισ.def: βασιληίς (poet. fem. of βασίλειος) royal, Il., Eur.

βασιλιζω.gloss: to be of the king's party
βασιλιζω.def: βασιλίζω (βασιλεύς) to be of the king's party, Plut.

βασιλικοσ.def: βασιλικός (like βασίλειος) I. royal, kingly, Hdt., attic 2. like a king, kingly, princely, βασιλικώτατος Xen.:—adv., βασιλικῶς as a king, with kingly authority, id. II. as Subst., 1. βασιλική (sub. στοά), a colonnade at Athens, Plat.; v. στοά. 2. βασιλικός, ὁ, king's officer, NTest.

βασιλισ.def: βασιλίς (= βασίλεια) 1. a queen, princess, Soph., Eur., etc. 2. as adj. royal, id.

βασισ.def: βάσις (βαίνω) I. a stepping, step, and collectively steps, Aesch., Soph., etc.; οὐκ ἔχων βάσιν power to step, id.; τροχῶν βάσεις the rolling of the wheels, id. II. that with which one steps, a foot, Eur., NTest. III. that whereon one stands, a base, Plat.

βασκαινω.def: βασκαίνω I. c. acc. to slander, malign, belie, disparage, Dem. 2. c. dat. to envy, grudge, id. II. to bewitch, by means of spells: Pass., ὡς μὴ βασκανθῶ (aor1 subj.) that I be not bewitched, Theocr.

βασκανια.def: βασκανία (from βάσκανος) slander, envy, malice, Plat., Dem.

βασκανοσ.def: βάσκανος (deriv. uncertain) I. slanderous, envious, malignant, Ar., Dem. II. as Subst. a slanderer, id. 2. a sorcerer, id.

βασκασ.def: βασκάς a kind of duck, Ar.

βασκω.def: βάσκω (akin to βαίνω, cf. χάσκω, χαίνω) (only used in imperat.) βάσκ’ ἴθι speed thee! away! Il.; also come! Aesch.

βασσαρα.def: βασσάρα (= ἀλώπηξ) (Prob. a foreign word.) I. a fox. II. a Thracian bacchanal, Anth.

βασσαριον.def: βασσάριον (Dim. of βασσάρα I) a little fox, Hdt.

βασταγμα.gloss: that which is borne, a burden
βασταγμα.def: βάσταγμα (from βαστάζω) that which is borne, a burden, Eur.

βασταζω.def: βαστάζω (Deriv. uncertain.) I. to lift, lift up, raise, Od., Soph., Eur.: to bear, carry, support, Aesch., Soph. 2. to hold in one's hands, id. 3. βαστάζειν ἐν γνώμηι to bear in mind, consider, weigh, make proof of, Aesch. II. to carry off, take away, NTest. III. attic also = ψηλαφάω, to touch, Aesch.

βαστακτοσ.def: βαστακτός (verb. adj. of βαστακτός) to be borne, Anth.

βαταλοσ.def: βάταλος (βάττος) a nickname given to Demosthenes, from his stuttering, Aeschin.

βατεω.def: βατέω (βαίνω) to tread, cover, of animals, Theocr.

βατηρισ.def: βατηρίς (βατέω) κλῖμαξ β. a mounting ladder, Anth.

βατισ.def: βατίς a flat fish, perhaps the skate, Ar.

βατοσ.def: βάτος a bramble-bush or wild raspberry, Od.
βάτος the Hebrew measure bath, = attic μετρητής, NTest.

βατραχειοσ.def: βατράχειος (βάτραχος) of or belonging to a frog: βατράχεια (sc. χρώματα), frog-colour, pale-green, Ar.

βατραχομυομαχια.gloss: the battle of the frogs and mice
βατραχομυομαχια.def: βατραχομυομαχία (From βάτραχος, μῦς, μάχη) the battle of the frogs and mice

βατραχοσ.def: βάτραχος (deriv. uncertain) a frog, Batr., Hdt., etc.

βαττολογεω.gloss: to speak stammeringly, say the same thing over and over again
βαττολογεω.def: βαττολογέω (From Βάττος) (λόγος) to speak stammeringly, say the same thing over and over again, NTest.

βαττοσ.def: Βάττος (Formed from the sound.) stammerer, name of a king of Cyrene, Hdt.

βαυζω.def: βαύζω (Formed from the sound.) (only in pres.) to cry βαά βαά, to bark, Theocr.: of angry persons, to snarl, yelp, Aesch.; trans. to shriek aloud for, τινά id.

βαφη.def: βαφή (βάπτω) I. a dipping of red-hot iron in water, the temper produced thereby, Arist. II. a dipping in dye, dyeing, dye, Aesch., Plat., etc.; κρόκου βαφαί the saffron- dyed robe, Aesch.; βαφαὶ ὕδρας the robe dipped in the hydra's blood, Eur. III. χαλκοῦ βαφαί, in Aesch., is prob. the art of tempering brass, to express something which no woman could know. IV. in Soph. Aj., βαφῆι σίδηρος ὥς must be construed not with ἐθηλύνθην, but with the preceding words καρτερὸς γενόμενος, for iron becomes harder, not softer, by being dipped.

βδαλλω.def: βδάλλω (Root ΒΔΑΛ) to milk cows, Plat.: to suck, Arist.

βδελλα.def: βδέλλα (from βδάλλω) a leech, Hdt., Theocr.

βδελυγμα.def: βδέλυγμα (βδελύσσομαι) an abomination, i. e. an idol, NTest.

βδελυρευομαι.gloss: to behave in a brutal manner
βδελυρευομαι.def: βδελυρεύομαι (from βδελυρός) Dep. to behave in a brutal manner, Dem.

βδελυρια.gloss: brutal conduct, want of shame and decency, brutality
βδελυρια.def: βδελυρία (from βδελυρός) brutal conduct, want of shame and decency, brutality, Oratt.

βδελυροσ.def: βδελυρός (βδέω) loathsome, disgusting, brutal, Ar., Oratt.; Sup. -ώτατος, Dem.

βδελυσσομαι.gloss: to feel nausea, to be sick
βδελυσσομαι.def: βδελύσσομαι (βδέω) I. to feel nausea, to be sick, Ar. 2. c. acc. to feel a loathing at, to loath, id. II. to be loathsome: οἱ ἐβδελυγμένοι the abominable (in ref. to βδέλυγμα), NTest.

βδυλλω.def: βδύλλω (from βδέω) 1. Lat. oppedere, to insult grossly, τινά Ar. 2. to be afraid of, id.

βεβαιοσ.def: βέβαιος (βαίνω) I. firm, steady, steadfast, sure, certain, Aesch., etc.; βεβαιότερος κίνδυνος a surer game, Thuc. 2. of persons, steadfast, steady sure, constant, Aesch., etc.; c. inf., βεβαιότεροι μηδὲν νεωτεριεῖν more certain to make no change, Thuc. 3. τὸ βέβαιον certainty, firmness, resolution, Hdt., Thuc. II. adv. -ως, Aesch., etc.; comp. -ότερον, Thuc.; Sup. -ότατα, id.

βεβαιοτησ.def: βεβαιότης (from βέβαιος) firmness, steadfastness, stability, assurance, certainty, Thuc., Plat.

βεβαιοω.gloss: to make firm, confirm, establish, secure, warrant, make good
βεβαιοω.def: βεβαιόω (from βέβαιος) I. to make firm, confirm, establish, secure, warrant, make good, Plat., Xen.; ἔργωι βεβαιούμενα things warranted by fact, opp. to ἀκοῆι λεγόμενα, Thuc. 2. β. τί τινι to secure one the possession of a thing, id.:—Mid. to establish for oneself, to confirm, secure, id. II. Mid. also to secure one's ground in argument, to asseverate, maintain, make good, Plat. 2. to guarantee a title, Isae.

βεβηλοσ.gloss: allowable to be trodden, permitted to human use
βεβηλοσ.def: βέβηλος (βηλός, with βε- as a redupl.) I. allowable to be trodden, permitted to human use, Lat. profanus, Soph., Eur.; ἐν βεβήλωι Thuc. II. of persons, unhallowed, impure, id., Plat.: c. gen. uninitiated in rites, Anth.

βεβολημαι.def: βεβόλημαι to be stricken with grief, Hom.; βεβολήατο epic 3rd pl. plup.

βεβουλευμενωσ.def: βεβουλευμένως (part. perf. pass. of βουλεύομαι,) advisedly, designedly, Dem.

βεκκεσεληνοσ.def: βεκκεσέληνος (A word coined from the story about βέκος in Hdt. 2. 2, and the Arcadian claim of being προσέληνοι.) (σελήνη) superannuated, doting, Ar.

βεκοσ.def: βεκός bread, a Phrygian word, Hdt.

βελεμνον.def: βέλεμνον poet. for βέλος, a dart, javelin, Il., Aesch.

βελονη.def: βελόνη (βέλος) any sharp point, a needle, Batr., Aeschin.

βελοσ.def: βέλος (βάλλω, as Lat. jaculum from jacio) 1. a missile, esp. an arrow, dart, bolt, Hom.; of the rock hurled by the Cyclops, Od.; of the ox's leg thrown at Ulysses, id.; ὑπὲκ βελέων out of the reach of darts, out of shot, Il.; so ἔξω βελῶν Xen. 2. like ἔγχος, used of any weapon, as a sword, Ar.: an axe, Eur. 3. the ἀγανὰ βέλεα of Apollo and Artemis in Hom. always denote the sudden, easy death of men and women respectively. 4. after Hom. of anything swift-darting, Ζηνὸς βέλη the bolts of Zeus, thunderbolts, Aesch.; πύρπνουν β. id.; βέλη πάγων the piercing frosts, Soph.:—metaph., ὀμμάτων βέλος the glance of the eye, Aesch.; ἱμέρου βέλος the shaft of love, id.; of arguments, πᾶν τετόξευται βέλος id.

βελοσφενδονη.gloss: a dart wrapped with pitch and tow, and thrown while on fire
βελοσφενδονη.def: βελοσφενδόνη a dart wrapped with pitch and tow, and thrown while on fire, Plut.

βελτεροσ.def: βέλτερος (Prob. from same Root as βούλομαι.) (poet. comp. and superl. of ἀγαθός) better, more excellent, βέλτερόν [ἐστι] it is better, c. inf., Hom.; in Theogn., Aesch., etc.

βελτιστοσ.def: βέλτιστος (cf. βέλτερος.) best, Ar., Plat., etc.:— ὦ βέλτιστε or βέλτιστε, a common mode of address, my good friend, Ar., etc.:— τὸ βέλτιστον the best, what is best, Aesch., Plat.:— οἱ βέλτιστοι or τὸ βέλτιστον the aristocracy, Lat. optimates, Xen.

βελτιων.def: βελτίων (attic comp. of ἀγαθός) (Cf. βέλτερος) better, ἐπὶ τὸ βέλτιον χωρεῖν to improve, advance, Thuc.

βεμβικιαω.def: βεμβικιάω (βέμβιξ) (only in pres.) to spin like a top, Ar.

βεμβικιζω.def: βεμβικίζω (βέμβιξ) to set a spinning, Ar.

βεμβιξ.def: βέμβιξ Lat. turbo, a top spun by whipping, Ar.

βενδιδεια.def: Βενδίδεια the festival of Bendis, Plat.

βενδιδειον.def: Βενδίδειον (from Βενδῖς) the temple of Bendis, Xen.

βενθοσ.def: βένθος (poet. for βάθος, as πένθος for πάθος) the depth of the sea, Hom.; also in pl., θαλάσσης βένθεα, ἐν βένθεσσιν ἁλός Il., Hom.:—also of a wood, βένθεσιν ὕλης Od.

βεομαι.def: βέομαι (Homeric fut. with no pres. in use) I shall live (akin to βιόω):— others regard it epic fut. of βαίνω.

βη.def: βῆ baa, the cry of sheep, Cratin.

βηλοσ.gloss: that on which one treads, the threshold
βηλοσ.def: βηλός (βαίνω) that on which one treads, the threshold, Lat. limen, Il., Aesch.

βημα.def: βῆμα (βαίνω) I. a step, pace, stride, Hhymn., Aesch., Eur.; Διὸς εὔφρονι βήματι under the kindly guidance of Zeus, Soph. II. = βάθρον, a step, seat, id.:— a raised place or tribune to speak from in a public assembly or law-court, Thuc., Oratt.

βησσα.def: βῆσσα (deriv. uncertain) a wooded comb or glen, Hom., Soph.

βησσηεισ.def: βησσήεις (from βῆσσα) of or like a glen, wooded, Hes.

βησσω.def: βήσσω (Formed from the sound.) (fut. βήξω Hipp.) to cough, Hdt.

βητα.def: βῆτα Β, β,, indecl., second letter of the Gr. alphabet: hence as numeral, βʹ δύο, δεύτερος, ͵β 2000. I. β is the medial labial mute, between tenuis τ and asp. θ. The dialectic variations of β seem to be mostly due to uncertainties of pronunciation: 1. for γ, as βλήχων γληχών, βλέφαρον doric γλέφαρον, βουνός γουνός· βεμβράς for μεμβράς, βροτός for μορτός (mortalis). 2. β is sometimes inserted between μλ, μρ to give a fuller sound, as in ἄμβροτος, μεσημβρία, γαμβρός, μέμβλεται.

βηταρμων.def: βητάρμων (Perh. from βαίνω ἀρμός.) a dancer, Od.

βια.def: βία I. bodily strength, force, power, might, Hom., etc.; periphr. βίη Ἡρακληείη the strength of Hercules, i. e. the strong Hercules, Il.; βίη Διομήδεος id.; Τυδέως βία, Πολυνείκους β. Aesch., etc. 2. of the mind, Il. II. force, an act of violence, Od.; in pl., id.; in attic, βίαι τινός against one's will, in spite of him, Aesch., Thuc., etc.; βίαι φρενῶν Aesch.; also βίαι alone as an adv., perforce, Od., etc.; so, πρὸς βίαν τινός and πρὸς βίαν alone, Aesch.

βιαζω.def: βιάζω (βία) I. to constrain, Od.:—Pass., aor1 ἐβιάσθην, perf. βεβίασμαι:— to be hard pressed or overpowered, Il.; βιάζομαι τάδε I suffer violence herein, Soph.; βιασθείς id.; ἐπεὶ ἐβιάσθη Thuc.; βεβιασμένοι forcibly made slaves, Xen.:—of things, τοὔνειδος βιασθέν forced from one, Soph. II. Mid. βιάζομαι, with aor1 mid. ἐβιασάμην, perf. βεβίασμαι:— to overpower by force, press hard, Hom.; βιάζεσθαι νόμους to do them violence, Thuc.;— β. αὑτόν to lay violent hands on oneself, Plat.:— β. τινα, c. inf., to force one to do, Xen.; and inf. omitted, β. τὰ σφάγια to force the victims [to be favourable], Hdt. 2. c. acc. rei, βιάζεσθαι τὸν ἔκπλουν to force the entrance, Thuc. 3. absol. to use force, struggle, Aesch., Soph., etc.: to force one's way, Thuc., Xen.; c. inf., β. πρὸς τὸν λόφον ἐλθεῖν Thuc.: of a famine, to increase in violence, Hdt.

βιαιομαχασ.def: βιαιομάχας (from βία, μάχομαι) fighting violently, Anth.

βιαιοσ.def: βίαιος (βία) I. forcible, violent, ἔργα βίαια Od.; β. θάνατος a violent death, Hdt., Plat., etc.; ὁ πόλεμος β. διδάσκαλος is a teacher of violence, Thuc.:—adv., βιαίως by force, perforce, Od., Aesch., etc.; so, πρὸς τὸ βίαιον id. II. pass. constrained, compulsory, Plat.

βιαρκησ.def: βιαρκής (βίος, ἀρκέω) supplying the necessaries of life, Anth.

βιαστεοσ.def: βιαστέος one must do violence to, Eur.

βιαστησ.gloss: one who uses force, a violent man
βιαστησ.def: βιαστής (βιάζω) one who uses force, a violent man, NTest.

βιαω.def: βιάω (= βιάζω) I. to constrain, Il.:— Pass. to be forcibly driven, of fire, Hdt.; θανάτωι βιηθείς overpowered, id. II. as Dep. in act. sense, to constrain, press hard, overpower, Hom.; βιήσατο κῦμ’ ἐπὶ χέρσου it forced me upon land, Od.; νῶϊ βιήσατο μισθόν he did us wrong in respect of our wages, Il.:— to force or urge on, Aesch.

βιβαζω.gloss: to make to mount, to lift up, exalt
βιβαζω.def: βιβάζω Causal of βαίνω, to make to mount, to lift up, exalt, Soph.

βιβασθω.def: βιβάσθω (= βιβάω, βίβημι, μακρὰ βιβάσθων long) striding, Il.

βιβαω.def: βιβάω (poet. form of βαίνω) to stride, πέλωρα βιβᾶι he takes huge strides, Hhymn.; ἐβίβασκε, 3rd sg. ionic imperf., id.; elsewhere in part., μακρὰ βιβῶντα, μακρὰ βιβῶσα Hom.

βιβημι.def: βίβημι to stride, only in part., μακρὰ βιβάς Il.

βιβλινοσ.def: βίβλινος βίβλινος, οἶνος, Biblian wine, from Biblis in Thrace, Hes., Theocr.: βύβλινος in Eur.

βιβλιοκαπηλοσ.def: βιβλιοκάπηλος a dealer in books, Luc.

βιβλιον.def: βιβλίον (Dim. of βίβλος) a paper, scroll, letter, Hdt., Ar., etc.; often written βυβλίον.

βιβλοσ.gloss: the inner bark of the papyrus
βιβλοσ.def: βίβλος (Prob. a foreign word.) I. the inner bark of the papyrus (βύβλος): generally, bark, Plat. II. a book, of which the leaves were made of this bark, Dem.

βιβρωσκω.def: βιβρώσκω (The Root is ΒΟΡ, v. βορά, Lat. voro.) to eat, eat up, βεβρωκὼς κακὰ φάρμακ’ Il.: c. gen. to eat of a thing, βεβρωκὼς βοός Od.:—Pass. to be eaten, χρήματα βεβρώσεται will be devoured, id.

βικοσ.def: βῖκος Oriental word for a wine-jar, Hdt., Xen.

βινεω.def: βινέω coire, of illicit intercourse, Ar.

βιοδοτησ.def: βιοδότης giver of life or food, Plat.

βιοδωροσ.def: βιόδωρος life-giving, Poeta ap. Plat., Soph.

βιοσ.def: βίος I. life, i. e. not animal life (ζωή), but a course of life, manner of living, Lat. vita, Od., etc.; in pl., τίνες καὶ πόσοι εἰσὶ βίοι; Plat. 2. in Poets = ζωή, βίον ἐκπνεῖν Aesch.; ἀποψύχειν Soph. 3. life-time, Hdt., Plat. II. a living, livelihood, means of living, substance, Lat. victus, Hes., Soph., etc.; τὸν βίον ποιεῖσθαι ἀπό τινος to make one's living of a thing, Thuc., etc. III. a life, biography, as those of Plut.

βιοστερησ.gloss: reft of the means of life
βιοστερησ.def: βιοστερής (στερέω) reft of the means of life, Soph.

βιοτεια.def: βιοτεία (βιοτή) a way of life, Xen.

βιοτευω.def: βιοτεύω (From βιοτή) 1. to live, Eur. 2. to get food, Thuc.: to live by or off a thing, ἀπὸ πολέμου Xen.

βιοτη.def: βιοτή I. = βίοτος, βίος, Od., attic Poets. II. a living, sustenance, Soph., Ar.

βιοτιον.def: βιότιον (Dim. of βίοτος) a scant living, Ar.

βιοτοσ.def: βίοτος (= βίος I) (βιόω) I. life, Il., Trag. II. = βίος II, means of living, substance, Lat. victus, Hom. III. the world, mankind, Anth.

βιοω.def: βιόω (βίος) to live, pass one's life (whereas ζάω properly means to live, exist), Il., etc.; ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὧν αὐτὸς βεβίωκεν from the very actions of his own life, Dem.; hence in Pass., τὰ σοὶ κἀμοὶ βεβιωμένα the actions of our life, id.; impers., βεβίωταί μοι I have lived, Lat. vixi, id.:—Mid. in act. sense, Hdt.

βιωσιμοσ.def: βιώσιμος (βιόω) to be lived, worth living, Eur.; οὐ βιώσιμόν ἐστί τινι ’tis not meet for him to live, Hdt., Soph.

βιωσκομαι.def: βιώσκομαι to quicken, make or keep alive, Od.

βιωτεοσ.def: βιωτέος (verb. adj. of βιόω) one must live, Plat.

βιωτικοσ.def: βιωτικός (βιόω) of or pertaining to life, NTest.

βιωτοσ.def: βιωτός (βιόω) to be lived, worth living, Soph., Ar., etc.

βλαβεροσ.def: βλαβερός (From βλάβη) (βλάπτω) hurtful, noxious, disadvantageous, Hes., Xen.

βλαβη.def: βλάβη (βλάπτω) 1. hurt, harm, damage, opp. to wilful wrong (ἀδίκημα), Aesch., etc.:— βλ. τινός damage to a person or thing, φορτίων Ar.; but, βλάβη θεοῦ mischief from a god, Eur.:—of a person, ἡ πᾶσα βλάβη who is naught but mischief, Soph. 2. βλάβης δίκη an action for damage done, Dem., etc.

βλαισοσ.gloss: having the knees bent inwards, bandylegged
βλαισοσ.def: βλαισός having the knees bent inwards, bandylegged, Lat. valgus, Batr., Xen.:—generally, twisted, crooked, Anth.

βλαισωσισ.def: βλαίσωσις (as if from βλαισόω) distortion, retortion, Arist.

βλακευω.def: βλακεύω (βλάξ) I. only in pres., to be slack, lazy, Xen. II. c. acc. to lose or waste through laziness, Luc.

βλακικοσ.def: βλακικός (βλάξ) lazy, stupid, Plat.: adv. -κῶς, Ar.

βλαξ.def: βλάξ (μαλακός) slack in body and mind, stupid, a dolt, Plat., Xen.:—Sup. βλακίστατος.

βλαπτω.def: βλάπτω (Root ΒΛΑΒ, v. βλάβη) I. to disable, hinder, stop Hom.:—βλ. πόδας to disable the feet, to lame them, Od.:—Pass., ὄζωι ἔνι βλαφθέντε [the horses] caught in a branch, Il.; βλάβεν ἅρματα were stopped, id.; Διόθεν βλαφθέντα βέλεμνα stopped, made frustrate by Zeus, id. 2. c. gen. to hinder from, βλάπτουσι κελεύθου Od.:—Pass., βλαβέντα λοισθίων δρόμων arrested in its last course, Aesch. II. of the mind, to distract, delude, deceive, mislead, of the Gods, Hom.; βλαφθείς, Lat. mente captus, Il. III. after Hom. to damage, hurt, mar, opp. to wilful wrong (ἀδικεῖν), Aesch., etc.

βλαστανω.def: βλαστάνω 1. to bud, sprout, grow, of plants, Aesch., etc. 2. metaph. to shoot forth, come to light, of men; ἀνθρώπου φύσιν βλαστών born in man's nature, Soph.; βλαστάνει ἀπιστία id. (The Root is ΒΛΑΣΤ, v. βλαστεῖν, βλαστή.)

βλαστεω.def: βλαστέω late form of βλαστάνω, often introduced by Copyist for the aor2 forms βλαστεῖν, βλαστών.

βλαστη.def: βλάστη I. = βλαστός, Plat., etc.; πετραία βλ. the growing rock, Soph. II. of children, βλάσται πατρός, birth from a father, id.; παιδὸς βλάσται its growth, id.

βλαστημα.def: βλάστημα I. = βλάστη I, Eur. II. metaph. offspring, an offshoot, Aesch., Eur. III. an eruption on the skin, Aretae.

βλαστοσ.def: βλαστός (βλαστάνω) a sprout, shoot, sucker, Lat. germen, Hdt.

βλασφημεω.def: βλασφημέω (βλάσφημος) 1. to drop evil or profane words, speak lightly or amiss of sacred things, βλ. εἰς θεούς Plat.: to utter ominous words, Aeschin. 2. to speak ill or to the prejudice of one, to speak slander, περί τινος Dem.; εἴς τινα id.:—also, βλ. τινα Babr., NTest.:—Pass. to have evil spoken of one, id. 3. to speak impiously or irreverently of God, to blaspheme, id.

βλασφημια.def: βλασφημία (From βλάσφημος) 1. a profane speech, opp. to εὐφημία, Eur., Plat. 2. defamation, evil-speaking, slander, Dem. 3. impious and irreverent speech against God, blasphemy, NTest.; τοῦ πνεύματος against the Spirit, id.; πρός τινα id.

βλασφημοσ.def: βλάσφημος (The origin of βλας is uncertain: βλάξ and βλάπτω have both been suggested.) 1. evil-speaking: of words, slanderous, Dem. 2. speaking blasphemy, blasphemous, and as Subst. a blasphemer, NTest.

βλαυτη.def: βλαύτη (deriv. uncertain) a kind of slipper worn by fops, Plat.

βλεμεαινω.def: βλεμεαίνω (deriv. uncertain) to look fiercely, glare around, Il.

βλεμμα.def: βλέμμα (βλέπω) a look, glance, Eur., Ar.

βλεπτεοσ.def: βλεπτέος (verb. adj. of βλέπω) one must look, Plat.

βλεπτικοσ.def: βλεπτικός of or for sight, Anth.

βλεπτοσ.def: βλεπτός (From βλέπω) to be seen, worth seeing, Soph.

βλεπω.gloss: to see, have the power of sight
βλεπω.def: βλέπω I. to see, have the power of sight, Soph.; μὴ βλέπηι ὁ μάντις lest he see too clearly, id. II. to look, εἴς τινα or τι, Aesch., etc.; πῶς βλέπων; with what face? Soph.;—with an adv., ἐχθρῶς βλ. πρός τινα Xen.:—foll. by a noun, φόβον βλ. to look terror, i. e. to look terrible, Aesch.; ἔβλεψε νᾶπυ looked mustard, Ar.; πυρρίχην βλέπων looking like a war-dancer, id.; πεφροντικὸς βλέπειν to look thoughtful, Eur. 2. to look to some one from whom help is expected, Soph.; εἴς τινα id., etc.:— of places, οἰκία πρὸς μεσημβρίαν βλέπουσα looking towards the south, Xen. 3. to look longingly, expect eagerly, c. inf., Ar. 4. to look to, ἑαυτούς NTest.; also, βλ. ἀπό τινος to beware of.., id.; βλ. ἵνα.. to see that.., id. III. trans. to see, behold, c. acc., Trag.: βλ. φάος, φῶς ἡλίου to see the light of day, to live, Aesch., Eur.; and, without φάος, to be alive, live, Aesch., etc.; of things, βλέποντα actually existing, id.

βλεφαρισ.def: βλεφαρίς an eyelash, in pl. eyelashes, Lat. cilia, Ar., Xen., etc.

βλεφαρον.def: βλέφαρον (βλέπω) (γλέφαρον is variously listed as Doric and Aeolic.) I. mostly in pl. the eyelids, Hom. II. the eyes, Trag.: ἁμέρας βλέφαρον, νυκτὸς βλέφαρον, i. e. the sun, the moon, Soph., Eur.

βλημα.def: βλῆμα (βάλλω) 1. a throw, cast, of dice, Eur. 2. a shot, wound, Hdt. 3. a coverlet, Anth.

βλητεοσ.def: βλητέος (verb. adj. of βάλλω) one must put, NTest.

βλητρον.def: βλῆτρον (βάλλω?) a fastening, a band or rivet, Il.

βληχαομαι.def: βληχάομαι (From βληχή) Dep. to bleat, of sheep and goats, Ar.; of infants, id.

βληχη.def: βληχή (Formed from the sound.) a bleating, οἰῶν Od.: the wailing of children, Eur.

βληχροσ.def: βληχρός (cf. ἀβληχρός) (βλάξ) weak, faint, slight, Plut.: cf. ἀ-βληχρός.

βληχωνιασ.def: βληχωνίας (from βλήχων) prepared with pennyroyal, Ar.

βλιττω.gloss: to cut out the comb of bees, take the honey
βλιττω.def: βλίττω (The Root is ΒΛΙΤ of μέλιτος, gen. of μέλι, β being in place of μ, cf. βλώσκω for μλώσκω).) to cut out the comb of bees, take the honey, Plat.:—metaph., βλ. τὸν δῆμον to rob the people of their honey, Ar.:—Pass., μέλι βλίττεται Plat.

βλοσυροσ.def: βλοσυρός (deriv. uncertain) grim, fierce, Il.: terrible, Aesch.: bluff, burly, valiant, Plat.

βλυζω.def: βλύζω gush forth; c. dat., βλ. Λυαίωι with wine, Anth.

βλωθροσ.def: βλωθρός (deriv. uncertain) tall, stately, of trees, Hom.

βλωσκω.def: βλώσκω (The Root is ΜΟΛ, so that βλώσκω is for μολώσκω, μλώσκω; cf. θρώσκω from ΘΟΡ.) (μέμβλωκα is for μεμόλωκα) to go or come, Hom., Trag.

βοαγριον.gloss: a shield of wild bull's hide
βοαγριον.def: βοάγριον (From βόαγρος) a shield of wild bull's hide, Il.

βοαω.def: βοάω (βοή) (a later form βοάσω in Eur. is aor1 subj) I. to cry aloud, to shout, Hom., Aesch.; οἱ βοησόμενοι men ready to shout (in the ἐκκλησία), Dem. 2. of things, to sound, resound, roar, howl, as the wind and waves, Il., Aesch.; αὐτὸ βοᾶι it proclaims itself, Ar. II. c. acc. pers. to call to one, call on, Eur., Xen. 2. to call for, shout out for, Soph. 3. c. acc. cogn., β. βοάν, μέλος, etc., Ar., Soph. 4. to noise abroad, βεβωμένα ἀνὰ Ἰωνίην Hdt.; ἐβώσθησαν ἀνὰ τὴν Ἑλλάδα id. 5. c. inf. to cry aloud or command in a loud voice to do a thing, Soph., Eur., Xen.

βοειη.def: βοείη sc.βοείη δορή, an ox-hide, ox-hide shield, Hom.; gen. pl. βοῶν, contr. for βοέων, Il.

βοεικοσ.def: βοεικός (= βόειος,) (βοῦς) of or for oxen, ζεύγη β. wagons drawn by oxen, Thuc., Xen.

βοειοσ.def: βόειος (βοῦς) of an ox or oxen, esp. of ox-hide, Hom.; βόεα κρέα Hdt.; γάλα βόειον cows milk, Eur.; metaph., βόεια ῥήματα great bull- words (cf. βούπαις, etc.), Ar.

βοευσ.def: βοεύς (βοῦς) a rope of ox-hide, Od.

βοη.def: βοή I. a loud cry, shout, Hom., etc.:— a battle-cry, βοὴν ἀγαθός good at the battle-cry, Il.; βοᾶς μηδ’ ὄνομ’ ἔστω let there be not even the name of war, Theocr.:—also of the roar of the sea, Od.; of the sound of musical instruments, Il., Pind.; the cry of birds or beasts, Soph., Eur.;— ὅσον ἀπὸ βοῆς ἕνεκεν as far as sound went, only in appearance, Thuc., Xen. II. = βοήθεια, aid called for, succour, Aesch., Soph.

βοηγενησ.def: βοηγενής (γίγνομαι) born of an ox, of bees, Anth.

βοηδρομεω.gloss: to run to a cry for aid, haste to help
βοηδρομεω.def: βοηδρομέω (βοηδρόμος) to run to a cry for aid, haste to help, Eur.

βοηδρομια.def: Βοηδρόμια (βοηδρόμος) games in memory of the succour given by Theseus against the Amazons, Dem., Plut.

βοηδρομιων.def: Βοηδρομιών the third Attic month, in which the Βοηδρόμια were celebrated, answering nearly to our September, Dem.

βοηδρομοσ.gloss: running to a cry for aid, giving succour, a helper
βοηδρομοσ.def: βοηδρόμος (βοή, δραμεῖν) running to a cry for aid, giving succour, a helper, Eur.: cf. βοηθόος.

βοηθεια.def: βοήθεια (From βοηθητέος) I. help, aid, rescue, support, Thuc., etc. 2. medical aid, cure, Plut. II. an auxiliary force, βοήθεια Thuc., Xen.

βοηθεω.gloss: to come to aid, to succour, assist, aid
βοηθεω.def: βοηθέω (βοηθός) 1. to come to aid, to succour, assist, aid, c. dat. pers., Hdt., Eur., etc.; πρός τινα Xen. 2. absol. to give aid, come to the rescue, Hdt., Thuc., etc.

βοηθητεοσ.def: βοηθητέος (βοηθέω) one must help, Xen., Dem.

βοηθοοσ.gloss: hasting to the battle-shout, hasting to battle
βοηθοοσ.def: βοηθόος (βοή, θέω) I. hasting to the battle-shout, hasting to battle, Il.; cf. βοηδρόμος. II. aiding, helping, Pind.; and as Subst. an assistant, Theocr.

βοηθοσ.def: βοηθός (shortened form of βοηθόος) assisting, auxiliary, Thuc.; and as Subst. an assistant, Hdt., Plat.

βοηλασια.def: βοηλασία (From βοηλάτης) I. a driving of oxen, cattle-lifting, Il. II. a cattle-run, Anth.

βοηλατησ.gloss: one that drives away oxen, a cattle-lifter
βοηλατησ.def: βοηλάτης (βοῦς, ἐλαύνω) I. one that drives away oxen, a cattle-lifter, Anth. II. ox-driving, id.

βοηλατικοσ.def: βοηλατικός (from βοηλάτης) of or for cattle-driving:— ἡ βοηλατική (sc. τέχνη) the herdsman's art, Plat.

βοητησ.def: βοητής (βοάω) clamorous:— doric fem. βοᾶτις Aesch.

βοθροσ.def: βόθρος (Prob. from the same Root as βαθύς: cp. also Lat. fodio.) any hole or pit dug in the ground, Lat. puteus, Hom.: a natural trough for washing clothes in, Od.:— a hole, such as a fire makes in the snow, Xen.

βοι.def: βοῖ like αἰβοῖ, exclam. of disgust, Ar.

βοιωταρχεω.def: Βοιωταρχέω (from Βοιωτάρχης) to be a Boeotarch, Thuc.

βοιωταρχησ.def: Βοιωτάρχης (ἄρχω) a Boeotarch, one of the chief magistrates at Thebes, Hdt., Thuc., etc.

βοιωταρχια.def: Βοιωταρχία (from Βοιωτάρχης) the office of Boeotarch, Plut.

βοιωτια.def: Βοιωτία (βοῦς) Boeotia, so called from its cattle-pastures, Hes.

βοιωτιαζω.gloss: to play the Boeotian, speak Boeotian, side with the Boeotians
βοιωτιαζω.def: Βοιωτιάζω (Βοιωτός) to play the Boeotian, speak Boeotian, side with the Boeotians, Xen.

βοιωτιοσ.def: Βοιώτιος Boeotian: the Boeotians were proverbially clownish, whence the saying ὗς Βοιωτία.

βολβοσ.def: βολβός a bulb: in Theocr. a truffle?

βολη.def: βολή (βάλλω) 1. a throw, the stroke or wound of a missile, opp. to πληγή (stroke of sword or pike), Od., Eur., Thuc.: βολαῖς σφόγγος ὤλεσεν γραφήν by its stroke or touch, Aesch. 2. metaph., like βέλος, a glance from the eyes, Od. 3. βολαὶ κεραύνιοι thunder- bolts, Aesch.; βολαὶ ἡλίου sun- beams, Soph.; βολὴ χιόνος a snow- shower, Eur.

βολιζω.gloss: to heave the lead, take soundings
βολιζω.def: βολίζω (From βολίς) to heave the lead, take soundings, NTest.

βολισ.def: βολίς (βάλλω) 1. a javelin, Plut. 2. a cast of the dice, a die, Anth.

βολιτον.def: βόλιτον (βάλλω?) cow-dung, mostly in pl., Ar.

βολοκτυπιη.def: βολοκτυπίη (κτύπος) the rattling of the dice, Anth.

βολοσ.gloss: a throw with a casting-net, a cast
βολοσ.def: βόλος (βάλλω) 1. a throw with a casting-net, a cast, Orac. ap. Hdt., Theocr.: metaph., εἰς βόλον καθίστασθαι to fall within the cast of the net, Eur. 2. the thing caught, a draft of fish, Aesch., id.

βομβαυλιοσ.def: βομβαύλιος (βομβέω, αὐλός) a bagpiper, with a play on βομβυλιός, Ar.

βομβεω.gloss: to make a booming, humming noise, to sound deep
βομβεω.def: βομβέω (βόμβος) to make a booming, humming noise, to sound deep or hollow, Hom.; βόμβησαν κατὰ ῥόον the oars fell with a loud noise down into the tide, Od.; βόμβησεν λίθος the stone flew humming through the air, id.:—of bees, to hum, Theocr.; of mosquitoes, to buzz, Ar.

βομβοσ.def: βόμβος (Formed from the sound.) a booming, humming, Plat.

βομβυλιοσ.def: βομβυλιός (from βόμβος) an insect that hums or buzzes, a bumble-bee, Ar.

βορα.def: βορά (v. βιβρώσκω) eatage, meat, properly of carnivorous beasts, Trag.; of cannibal-like feast, Hdt., Trag.:—rarely of simple food, Aesch., Soph.

βορβοροκοιτησ.def: Βορβοροκοίτης (κοίτη) mudcoucher, name of a frog, Batr.

βορβοροσ.def: βόρβορος mud, mire, Lat. coenum, Aesch., Ar., etc.

βορεασ.def: Βορέας (Prob. from ὄρος, ϝόρος, wind from the mountains.) the North wind, Lat. Aquilo, Od.; πρὸς βορῆν ἄνεμον towards the North, Hdt.; πρὸς βορέαν τινός northward of a place, Thuc.

βορειοσ.gloss: from the quarter of the North wind, northern
βορειοσ.def: βόρειος (from Βορέας) from the quarter of the North wind, northern, Hdt.; ἀκτὰ β. exposed to the north, Soph.

βορηιασ.def: Βορηιάς (from Βορέας) a Boread, daughter of Boreas, Soph.

βορυεσ.def: βόρυες unknown Libyan animals, Hdt.; cf. ὄρυες.

βορυσθενειτησ.gloss: an inhabitant of the banks of the Borysthenes
βορυσθενειτησ.def: Βορυσθενείτης an inhabitant of the banks of the Borysthenes, Hdt

βορυσθενησ.def: Βορυσθένης the Borysthenes or Dnieper, a river of Scythia, Hdt.

βοσκημα.def: βόσκημα (βόσκω) I. that which is fed or fatted: in pl. fatted beasts, cattle, Soph., etc.; of sheep, Eur.; of horses, id.; of pigs, Ar. II. food, Aesch.

βοσκητεοσ.def: βοσκητέος (verb. adj. of βόσκω) one must feed, Ar.

βοσκω.def: βόσκω I. of the herdsman, to feed, tend, Lat. pasco, Od. 2. generally, to feed, nourish, support, of earth, id.; of the Sun, Soph.; of soldiers, to maintain, Hdt., Thuc.: metaph., β. νόσον Soph.; πράγματα β. to feed up troubles, i. e. children, Ar. II. Pass., of cattle, to feed, graze, Lat. pascor, Hom., c. acc.:— to feed on, Aesch. 2. metaph. to be fed or nurtured, Trag.; β. τινί or περί τι to run riot in athing, Anth. (The Root appears to be ΒΟΤ, cf. βοτήρ, βοτός, βοτάνη.）

βοσποροσ.def: Βόσπορος ox-ford, name of several straits, of which the Thracian and Cimmerian are best known, Hdt.; also of the Hellespont, Aesch., Soph.

βοστρυχοσ.def: βόστρυχος (βότρυς) 1. a curl or lock of hair, Aesch., etc. 2. anything twisted or wreathed, πυρὸς β., of a flash of lightning, id.

βοτανη.def: βοτάνη (βόσκω) grass, fodder, Il., Plat.; ἐκ βοτάνης from feeding, from pasture, Theocr.

βοτηρ.def: βοτήρ (βόσκω) a herdsman, herd, Od.; οἰωνῶν β. a soothsayer, Aesch.; κύων βοτήρ a herdsman's dog, Soph.

βοτηρικοσ.def: βοτηρικός (from βοτήρ) of or for a herdsman, Plut., Anth.

βοτον.def: βοτόν (βόσκω) a beast, Aesch., Soph.: mostly in pl. grazing beasts, Il., Trag., etc.; but of birds, Ar.

βοτρυδον.gloss: like a bunch of grapes, in clusters
βοτρυδον.def: βοτρυδόν (βότρυς) like a bunch of grapes, in clusters, Il.

βοτρυοπαισ.def: βοτρυόπαις 1. grape-born, child of the grape, Anth. 2. act. bearing grapes, Theocr.

βοτρυσ.def: βότρυς (From same Root as βόστρυχος.) 1. a cluster or bunch of grapes, Il., attic 2. = βόστρυχος, Anth.

βοτρυχωδησ.def: βοτρυχώδης (from βότρυχος) (εἶδος) like curls, curly, Eur.

βοτρυωδησ.def: βοτρυώδης (εἶδος) like a bunch of grapes, Eur.

βου.def: βου- (from βοῦς, cf. ἵππος IV.) prefix often used in compos. to express something huge and monstrous, e. g. βούπαις, βουγάϊος.

βουβαλισ.def: βούβαλις an African species of antelope, prob. the hartbeeste, Hdt.

βουβρωστισ.def: βούβρωστις (βιβρώσκω) eating enormously: metaph. grinding poverty or misery, Il.

βουβων.def: βουβών the groin, Lat. inguen, Il.

βουβωνιαω.gloss: to suffer from swellings in the groin
βουβωνιαω.def: βουβωνιάω (from βούβων) to suffer from swellings in the groin, Ar.

βουγαιοσ.def: βουγάιος (γαίω) a great bully or braggart, voc. βουγάϊε Hom.

βουδοροσ.def: βουδόρος (δέρω) I. flaying oxen, Hes. II. as Subst. a knife for flaying, Babr.

βουθυσια.def: βουθυσία a sacrifice of oxen, Anth.

βουθυτεω.def: βουθυτέω (From βούθυτος) to slay or sacrifice oxen, Soph., Eur.: generally to sacrifice any animals, Ar.

βουθυτοσ.def: βούθυτος (θύω) 1. of or belonging to sacrifices, esp. of oxen, Aesch., Eur. 2. on which oxen are offered, sacrificial, Trag., Ar.

βουκερωσ.def: βούκερως (κέρας) horned like an ox or cow, Hdt., Aesch.

βουκεφαλασ.def: Βουκεφάλας the horse of Alexander the Great, Plut.

βουκεφαλοσ.def: βουκέφαλος (κεφαλή) bull-headed, epith. of Thessalian horses, Ar.

βουκολεω.def: βουκολέω (βουκόλος) I. to tend cattle, Il.:—Pass. of cattle, to range the fields, graze, id. 2. of persons, to tend, serve, worship, Ar.: Mid., τόνδε βουκολούμενος πόνον being constantly engaged in this toil, Aesch. II. metaph. to delude, beguile, id.; Mid., ἐλπίσι βουκολοῦμαι I feed myself on hopes, cheat myself with them, Eur.

βουκολημα.def: βουκόλημα (from βουκολέω) a beguilement, τῆς λύπης Babr.

βουκολια.def: βουκολία I. a herd of cattle, Hhymn., Hes. II. a byre, ox-stall, Hdt.

βουκολιαζομαι.def: βουκολιάζομαι (βουκόλος) Dep. to sing or write pastorals, Theocr.

βουκολιαστησ.def: βουκολιαστής (from βουκολιάζομαι) a pastoral poet, Theocr.

βουκολιον.def: βουκόλιον (From βουκόλος) I. a herd of cattle, Hdt., Theocr. II. a means of beguiling, Anth.

βουκολοσ.def: βουκόλος (-kolos is prob. an altered form of -πολος, cf. αἰπόλος.) a cowherd, herdsman, Hom., Plat.

βουλαιοσ.def: βουλαῖος (βουλή) of the council: βουλαία, a name of Vesta, as having a statue in the Senate House, Aeschin.

βουλαρχεω.def: βουλαρχέω to be a βούλαρχος, Arist.

βουλαρχοσ.def: βούλαρχος I. chief of the senate. II. adviser of a plan, Lat. auctor consilii, Aesch.

βουλευμα.gloss: a deliberate resolution, purpose, design, plan
βουλευμα.def: βούλευμα (βουλεύω) a deliberate resolution, purpose, design, plan, Hdt., attic

βουλευσισ.def: βούλευσις I. deliberation, Arist. II. the wrongful enrolment of a person among the public debtors, Dem.

βουλευτεοσ.def: βουλευτέος (verb. adj. of βουλεύω,) one must take counsel, Aesch., Soph., Thuc.

βουλευτηριον.def: βουλευτήριον (βουλεύω) I. a council-chamber, senate-house, Lat. curia, Hdt., attic II. the council or senate itself: and poet. a counsellor, Eur.

βουλευτησ.def: βουλευτής (βουλεύω) a councillor, senator, Il., Hdt., etc.;—at Athens, one of the 500, Oratt.

βουλευτικοσ.def: βουλευτικός (βουλεύω) I. of or for the council or the councillors, Xen., Dem. 2. able to advise or deliberate, Plat., etc. II. as Subst., βουλευτικόν, in the Athen. theatre, the seats next the orchestra, reserved for the Council, Ar. 2. the senatorial order, Plut.

βουλευω.gloss: to take counsel, deliberate, concert measures
βουλευω.def: βουλεύω (βουλή) I. to take counsel, deliberate, concert measures, and in past tenses to have considered and so to determine, resolve: 1. absol., οἷος ἔην βουλευέμεν ἠδὲ μάχεσθαι such as he was in council and in battle, Od.; ἔς γε μίαν βουλεύσομεν [sc. βουλήν] we shall agree to one plan, id.:—in Prose, this sense belongs chiefly to the Mid. 2. c. acc. rei, to deliberate on, plan, devise, Od., Hdt., attic:—Pass. with fut. mid., aor1 ἐβουλεύθην: perf. βεβούλευμαι:— to be determined or resolved on, Aesch., etc.; τὰ βεβουλευμένα βουλεύματα, Hdt. 3. c. inf. to resolve to do, Od., Hdt. II. to give counsel, τὰ λῷστα β. Aesch.; c. dat. pers. to advise, Il., Aesch. III. in polit. writers, to be a member of Council, Hdt.; esp. of the Council of 500 at Athens, Plat., Xen., etc. B. Mid., fut. -εύσομαι: aor1 ἐβουλευσάμην, epic βουλ or in pass. form ἐβουλεύθην: perf. βεβούλευμαι: 1. absol. to take counsel with oneself, deliberate, Hdt., attic 2. c. acc. rei, to determine with oneself, resolve on, Il., Hdt. 3. c. inf. to resolve to do, id., Plat.; β. ὅπως.., Xen.

βουλη.def: βουλή (βούλομαι) I. will, determination, Lat. consilium, esp. of the gods, Il., etc. 2. a counsel, piece of advice, plan, design, id., Hdt., attic:—in pl. counsels, Aesch. II. a Council of the elders or chiefs, a Senate, Hom., Aesch.:—at Athens, the Council of 500 created by Cleisthenes, Hdt., Ar., etc.:— βουλῆς εἶναι to be of the Council, a member of it, Thuc.

βουλησισ.def: βούλησις (βούλομαι) I. a willing: one's will, intention, purpose, Eur., Thuc., etc. II. the purpose or meaning of a poem, Plat.

βουλητοσ.def: βουλητός (βούλομαι) that is or should be willed: —τὸ β. the object of the will, Plat., Arist.

βουληφοροσ.def: βουληφόρος (φέρω) counselling, advising, Il.; c. gen. a counsellor, id.

βουλιμια.def: βουλιμία (βου-, λιμός) ravenous hunger, a disease, Arist.

βουλιμιαω.def: βουλιμιάω (from βουλιμία) to suffer from βουλιμία, Ar., Xen.

βουλομαι.def: βούλομαι (The Root is ΒΟΛ, which appears in epic βόλομαι, Lat.volo: hence βουλή.) Dep. I. to will, wish, be willing, Hom., etc.:—mostly c. inf. or c. acc. et inf., id., etc.: when βούλομαι is foll. by acc. only, an inf. may be supplied, Τρώεσσιν ἐβούλετο νίκην he willed victory to the Trojans, or Τρώεσσιν ἐβούλετο κῦδος ὀρέξαι, — both in Il. II. attic usages: 1. βούλει or βούλεσθε foll. by subj., adds force to the demand, βούλει λάβωμαι would you have me take hold, Soph. 2. εἰ βούλει, a courteous phrase, like Lat. sis (si vis), if you please, id. 3. ὁ βουλόμενος, Lat. quivis, the first that offers, Hdt., attic 4. βουλομένωι μοί ἐστι, nobis volentibus est, c. inf., it is according to my wish that.., Thuc. 5. to mean so and so, τί βούλεται εἶναι; quid sibi vult haec res? Plat.:—hence, βούλεται εἶναι professes or pretends to be, would fain be, id. III. followed by ἤ, to prefer, for βούλομαι μᾶλλον, βούλομ’ ἐγὼ λαὸν σόον ἔμμεναι, ἢ ἀπολέσθαι I had rather the people were saved than lost, Il.

βουλυτονδε.def: βουλυτόνδε (from βουλυτός) towards even, at eventide, Hom.

βουλυτοσ.gloss: the time for unyoking oxen, evening
βουλυτοσ.def: βουλυτός (λύω) the time for unyoking oxen, evening, Ar.

βουνιτησ.def: βουνίτης (βουνός) a dweller on the hills, Anth.

βουνοβατεω.def: βουνοβατέω (βαίνω) to walk the hills, Anth.

βουνομοσ.def: βούνομος (νέμομαι) (cf. βουνόμος) grazed by cattle, Soph.
βουνόμος (νέμομαι) (cf. βούνομος) ἀγέλαι βουνόμοι (parox.) herds of oxen at pasture, id.

βουπαισ.def: βούπαις (bou-, παῖς) I. a big boy, Ar. II. （βοῦς, παῖς) child of the ox, of bees, in allusion to their fabulous origin, Anth.

βουπαλειοσ.def: Βουπάλειος like Bupalus, i. e. stupid, Anth.

βουπαλισ.def: βούπαλις (πάλη) wrestling like a bull, i. e. hard-struggling, Anth.

βουπλαστησ.def: βουπλάστης (πλάσσω) cow-modeller, of the sculptor Myron, Anth.

βουπληξ.def: βουπλήξ (πλήσσω) 1. an ox-goad, Lat. stimulus, Il. 2. an axe for felling an ox, Anth.

βουποροσ.def: βουπόρος (πείρω) ox-piercing, βουπ. ὀβελός a spit large enough to spit an ox, Hdt., Eur.

βουπρωροσ.gloss: with the face of an ox
βουπρωροσ.def: βούπρῳρος (πρώιρα) with the face of an ox, Soph.

βουσ.def: βοῦς I. Lat. bos (bov-is), a bullock, bull, ox, or a cow, in pl. oxen or kine, cattle, Hom., etc. II. = βοείη or βοέη (always fem.), an ox-hide shield, Il. III. proverb., βοῦς ἐπὶ γλώσσηι βέβηκε, βοῦς ἐπὶ γλώσσης ἐπιβαίνει, of people who keep silence from some weighty reason, from the notion of a heavy body keeping down the tongue, Theogn., Aesch.

βουστροφοσ.def: βουστρόφος (στρέφω) ox-guiding, and as Subst. an ox-goad, Anth.

βουτησ.def: βούτης (βοῦς) I. a herdsman, Aesch., Eur., Theocr. II. as adj., βούτ. φόνος the slaughter of kine, Eur.

βουτομον.def: βούτομον (τεμεῖν) butomus, the flowering rush, Ar., Theocr.

βουφονια.def: βουφόνια (from βουφόνος) sc. βουφόνια ἱερά a festival with sacrifices of oxen, Ar.

βουφονοσ.def: βουφόνος (⁎φένω) I. ox-slaying, ox-offering, Hhymn. II. at or for which steers are slain, Aesch.

βουφορβια.def: βουφόρβια (from βουφορβός) a herd of oxen, Eur.

βουφορβοσ.def: βουφορβός (φέρβω) ox-feeding, and as Subst. a herdsman, Eur., Plat.

βουχανδησ.def: βουχανδής (χανδάνω) holding a whole ox, Anth.

βοωνησ.gloss: an officer who bought oxen for the sacrifices
βοωνησ.def: βοώνης (ὠνέομαι) at Athens, an officer who bought oxen for the sacrifices, Dem.

βοωπισ.def: βοῶπις (ὤψ) ox-eyed, i. e. having large, full eyes, mostly of Hera, Hom.

βοωτησ.def: βοώτης (βοῦς) I. a ploughman, Babr. II. the name given to the constellation Arcturus, Od.; v. ἄρκτος II.

βραβειον.def: βραβεῖον (from βραβεύς) a prize in the games, NTest.

βραβευσ.gloss: the judge who assigned the prizes at the games
βραβευσ.def: βραβεύς (deriv. uncertain) 1. the judge who assigned the prizes at the games, Lat. arbiter, Soph., Plat. 2. generally, an arbitrator, umpire, judge, Eur.: then a chief, leader, Aesch.: an author, Eur.

βραβευω.def: βραβεύω (βραβεύς) I. to act as a judge or umpire, Isocr. II. c. acc. to arbitrate, decide on, τὰ δίκαια Dem.:— to direct, arrange, control, Anth.

βραγχοσ.def: βραγχός (Prob. formed from the sound.) hoarse, Anth.
βράγχος (from βραγχός) hoarseness, or sore throat causing hoarseness, Thuc.

βραδυνω.def: βραδύνω (βραδύς) I. trans. to make slow, delay:— Pass. to be delayed, Soph. II. intr. to be long, to loiter, delay, id.: so in Mid., Aesch.

βραδυπουσ.def: βραδύπους slow of foot, slow, Eur.

βραδυσ.def: βραδύς I. slow, Hom., etc.:—c. inf., ἵπποι βάρδιστοι θείειν slowest at running, Il.; β. λέγειν Eur.:—adv., βραδέως χωρεῖν Thuc. 2. of the mind, like Lat. tardus, Il.; c. inf., προνοῆσαι βραδεῖς Thuc.; τὸ βραδύ slowness, id.:—adv., βραδέως βουλεύεσθαι id. II. of Time, tardy, late, Soph., Thuc.

βραδυτησ.def: βραδυτής (βραδύς) 1. slowness, Il., attic 2. of the mind, Plat.

βρασσω.def: βράσσω 1. to shake violently, throw up, of the sea, Anth. 2. to winnow grain, Plat.

βραχεα.def: βράχεα (as if from a nom. βράχος, or βραχέα (neut. pl. of βραχύς）) shallows, Lat. brevia, Hdt., Thuc.

βραχειν.def: βραχεῖν (found only in 3rdc sing. epic aor2 ἔβραχε or βράχε) to rattle, clash, ring, of arms; of a torrent, to roar; of an axle, to creak; of one wounded, to shriek or roar, — all in Il.

βραχιων.def: βραχίων (deriv. uncertain) the arm, Lat. brachium, Il.; πρυμνὸς βραχίων the shoulder, id.

βραχυβωλοσ.def: βραχύβωλος with small or few clods, Anth.

βραχυδρομοσ.def: βραχύδρομος (δραμεῖν, v. τρέχω) running a short way, Xen.

βραχυκωλοσ.def: βραχύκωλος (κῶλον) I. with short limbs or ends, Strab. II. consisting of short clauses, περίοδοι Arist.

βραχυλογια.def: βραχυλογία (from βραχυλόγος) brevity in speech or writing, Plat.

βραχυλογοσ.gloss: short in speech, of few words
βραχυλογοσ.def: βραχυλόγος (λέγω) short in speech, of few words, Plat.

βραχυνω.gloss: to shorten, to use as a short syllable
βραχυνω.def: βραχύνω fut. υνῶ, to shorten, to use as a short syllable, Plut.

βραχυποροσ.def: βραχύπορος 1. with a short passage, Plat. 2. with narrow passage, Plut.

βραχυσ.def: βραχύς short, Lat. brevis: 1. of Space and Time, Hdt., attic; ἐν βραχεῖ (ionic βραχέϊ) in a short time, briefly, Hdt., etc.; διὰ βραχέος Thuc.:—adv. βραχέως, scantily, seldom, id. 2. of Size, short, small, little, Pind., Soph.; βρ. τεῖχος a low wall, Thuc.; κατὰ βραχύ little by little, id. 3. of Quantity, few, διὰ βραχέων in few words, Plat.; διὰ βραχυτάτων Dem.:—adv., βραχέως, briefly, in few words, Xen. 4. of quality, humble, insignificant, Soph.:—of things, small, petty, trifling, id., etc.:—neut. as adv., βραχὺ φροντίζειν τινός to think lightly of, Dem.

βραχυσυμβολοσ.def: βραχυσύμβολος (σύμβολον) bringing a small contribution, Anth.

βραχυτησ.def: βραχύτης (βραχύς) 1. shortness, Thuc. 2. narrowness, deficiency, id.

βραχυτονοσ.def: βραχύτονος (τείνω) reaching but a short way, Plut.

βρεγμα.gloss: the front part of the head
βρεγμα.def: βρέγμα (deriv. uncertain) the front part of the head, Lat. sinciput, Batr.

βρεκεκεκεξ.def: βρεκεκεκέξ formed to imitate the croaking of frogs, Ar.

βρεμω.def: βρέμω (only in pres. and imperf.) (Lat. fremo) I. to roar, of a wave, Il.; so also in Mid., id., Soph. II. in later Poets, of arms, to clash, ring, Eur.; of men, to shout, rage, Aesch., Eur. to bear oneself haughtily, to hold one's head high, swagger, Ar., Plat.

βρετασ.gloss: a wooden image of a god
βρετασ.def: βρέτας (deriv. uncertain) a wooden image of a god, Aesch., Eur., Ar.

βρεφοσ.def: βρέφος I. the babe in the womb, Lat. foetus: of an unborn foal, Il. II. the new-born babe, Aesch., Eur.:—of beasts, a foal, whelp, cub, Hdt.:— ἐκ βρέφεος from babyhood, Anth.

βρεχμοσ.def: βρεχμός (= βρέγμα) the top of the head, Lat. sinciput, Il.

βρεχω.def: βρέχω I. Lat. rigo, to wet, τὸ γόνυ, of men walking through water, Hdt.:—Pass. to be wetted, get wet, βρεχόμενοι πρὸς τὸν ὀμφαλόν Xen.; βρέχεσθαι ἐν ὕδατι to bathe in water, Hdt.: of hard drinkers, βρεχθείς soaked, Eur. II. to rain, send rain, NTest.; c. acc. cogn., βρ. πῦρ to rain fire, id. 2. impers. βρέχει, like ὕει, Lat. pluit, it rains, id.

βριαρεωσ.def: βριάρεως (from βριαρός) a hundred-handed giant, so called by the gods, but by men Aegaeon, Il.

βριαροσ.def: βριαρός (From same Root as βριθύς, βρίθω, βαρύς.) strong, stout, Il.

βριαω.def: βριάω to make or to be strong and mighty, Hes. (v. βριαρός.）

βριζω.gloss: to be sleepy, to slumber, nod
βριζω.def: βρίζω (βριθύς) to be sleepy, to slumber, nod, Il., Aesch.

βριθυσ.def: βριθύς (Cf. βριαρός.) weighty, heavy, Il, Irreg. comp. βριθύτερος, Aesch.

βριθω.def: βρίθω (From same Root as βριαρός.) I. to be heavy or weighed down with a thing, c. dat., of fruit-trees, Hom.; metaph., ὄλβωι βρίθειν Eur.; ξίφεσι βρ. to visit heavily with the sword, id. 2. c. gen. to groan with weight of a thing, σίτου, οἴνου Od. 3. absol. to be heavy, Il.; rare in attic, βρίθει ὁ ἵππος sinks, Plat. II. of men, to outweigh, prevail, ἐέδνοισι by gifts, Od.: absol. to have the preponderance in fight, to be master, prevail, Il. III. trans. to weigh down, Aesch.:—Pass. to be laden, καρπῶι βριθομένη laden with fruit, Il.:—c. gen., βρίθεσθαι σταχύων Hes.

βριμαομαι.gloss: to snort with anger, to be indignant
βριμαομαι.def: βριμάομαι (from βρίμη) Dep. to snort with anger, to be indignant, Ar.

βριμη.def: βρίμη (From same Root as βριαρός.) strength, bulk, Hhymn.

βρομεω.def: βρομέω (= βρέμω) (only in pres. and imperf.) of flies, to buzz, Il.

βρομιοσ.def: Βρόμιος (from βρόμιος) 1. as a name of Bacchus, Aesch., Eur.; Βρομίου πῶμα, i. e. wine, id. 2. as adj. Βρόμιος, α, ον, Bacchic, id., Ar.

βρομοσ.def: βρόμος (βρέμω) 1. Lat. fremitus, any loud noise, as the crackling of fire, Il.; roaring of a storm, Aesch.; neighing of horses, id. 2. rage, fury, Eur.

βρονταω.def: βροντάω (from βροντή) 1. to thunder, Od.; metaph. of Pericles, Ar. 2. impers., βροντᾶι it thunders, id.

βροντη.def: βροντή (Akin to βρέμω, βρόμος.) I. thunder, Hom., etc. II. the state of one struck with thunder, astonishment, Hdt.

βροντησ.def: Βρόντης (βροντάω) thunderer, one of the three Cyclopes, Hes.

βροντησικεραυνοσ.def: βροντησικέραυνος sending thunder and lightning, Ar.

βροτειοσ.def: βρότειος (βροτός) mortal, human, of mortal mould, Trag.

βροτοκτονεω.def: βροτοκτονέω (from βροτοκτόνος) to murder men, Aesch.

βροτολοιγοσ.gloss: plague of man, bane of men
βροτολοιγοσ.def: βροτολοιγός plague of man, bane of men, of Ares, Hom.

βροτοομαι.def: βροτόομαι (βρότος) Pass., to be stained with gore, Od.

βροτοσ.gloss: blood that has run from a wound, gore
βροτοσ.def: βρότος (deriv. uncertain) blood that has run from a wound, gore, Hom.
βροτός (The orig. form seems to have been μορτός, cf. ἄμβροτος.) a mortal man, Hom., attic Poets.

βροτοσκοποσ.def: βροτοσκόπος (σκοπέω) taking note of man, Aesch.

βροτοστυγησ.def: βροτοστυγής (στυγέω) hated by men or man-hating, Aesch.

βροτοφεγγησ.def: βροτοφεγγής (φέγγος) giving light to men, Anth.

βροχθοσ.def: βρόχθος (deriv. uncertain) the throat, Theocr., Anth.

βροχισ.def: βροχίς I. Dim. of βρόχος, Anth. II. （βρέχω) an ink-horn, id.

βροχοσ.def: βρόχος a noose or slip-knot, for hanging or strangling, Od., Hdt., Soph.:— a snare for birds, Ar.:— the mesh of a net; metaph., ληφθέντες ἐν ταὐτῶι βρόχωι Aesch.

βροχω.def: βρόχω to gulp down, a Root only found in aor1 ἔβροξα, Anth.:—used by Hom. only in compds., 1. ἀναβρόξαι, to swallow again, suck down again, ὅτ’ ἀναβρόξειε ὕδωρ, of Charybdis, Od.; and in aor2 part. pass., ὕδωρ ἀναβροχέν id. 2. καταβρόξαι, to gulp down, ὃς τὸ καταβρόξειε whoever swallowed the potion, id.

βρυκω.gloss: to eat with much noise, to eat greedily
βρυκω.def: βρύκω to eat with much noise, to eat greedily, Eur., Ar.:—metaph. to tear in pieces, devour, of a gnawing disease, Soph.; so in Pass., βρύκομαι, id., Anth.

βρυλλω.def: βρύλλω (from βρῦν) to cry for drink, of children, Ar.

βρυν.def: βρῦν (formed from the sound.) in Ar. βρῦν εἰπεῖν to say bryn, cry for drink.

βρυον.def: βρύον (βρύω) a kind of mossy sea-weed, Theocr.

βρυχαομαι.def: βρυχάομαι (cf. μυκάομαι, μέμυκα) Dep., to roar, bellow, Lat. rugire, of a bull, Soph., Ar.; of elephants, Plut.:—in Il. mostly of the death-cry of wounded men, κεῖτο βεβρυχώς; so, βρυχώμενον σπασμοῖσι, of Hercules, Soph.; δεινὰ βρυχηθείς id.:—in Od. of the roaring of waves. (Formed from the sound.) Hence

βρυχηδον.def: βρυχηδόν (βρύχω) with gnashing of teeth, Anth.

βρυχημα.def: βρύχημα bellowing, roaring, of men, Plut.

βρυχιοσ.gloss: from the depths of the sea
βρυχιοσ.def: βρύχιος (From ⁎βρύξ, of which an acc. βρύχα occurs in late poets; cf. ὑποβρύχιος.) from the depths of the sea, Aesch.; of thunder from the deep, id.

βρυω.def: βρύω (mostly in pres.) 1. to be full to bursting: 1. c. dat. to swell or teem with, βρύει ἄνθεϊ teems with bloom, Il.:—metaph., βρύων μελίτταις καὶ προβάτοις Ar.; of men, θράσει βρύων Aesch. 2. c. gen. to be full of, βρύων δάφνης, ἐλαίας, ἀμπέλου Soph.: metaph., νόσου βρ. Aesch. 3. absol. to abound, grow luxuriantly, Soph.: of the earth, to teem with produce, Xen. 4. c. acc. cogn. to send forth water, NTest. (Akin to βλύω, βλύζω, and perh. to φλύω.）

βρωμα.gloss: that which is eaten, food, meat
βρωμα.def: βρῶμα (βιβρώσκω) that which is eaten, food, meat, Thuc., Plat., etc.

βρωμαομαι.def: βρωμάομαι (Formed from the sound.) Dep. to bray, Lat. rudere, βρωμησάμενος Ar.

βρωματομιξαπατη.gloss: the false pleasure of eating made dishes
βρωματομιξαπατη.def: βρωματομιξαπάτη the false pleasure of eating made dishes, Anth.

βρωσισ.def: βρῶσις (βιβρώσκω) I. meat, Od., Thuc., etc. II. eating, Plat. 2. corrosion, rust, NTest.

βρωτοσ.def: βρωτός (verb. adj. of βιβρώσκω,) to be eaten:— βρωτόν, meat, Eur., Xen.

βυβλινοσ.def: βύβλινος (βύβλος) made of byblus, Od., Hdt.

βυβλοσ.def: βύβλος 1. the Egyptian papyrus, the root and triangular stalk of which were eaten by the poor, Hdt. 2. its fibrous coats, as prepared for ropes, id.; cf. βύβλινος. 3. the outer coat of the papyrus, used for writing on, hence in pl. leaves of byblus, id. 4. a paper, book, id.; in this sense more commonly written βίβλος (q. v.):—pl. βύβλα, τά, Anth.

βυθιζω.def: βυθίζω (βυθός) to sink a ship: metaph. to sink or ruin men, NTest.

βυθιοσ.def: βύθιος I. in the deep, sunken, Luc., Anth. II. in or of the sea, τὰ βύθια (sc. ζῷα), water-animals, Anth. III. metaph. of sound, deep, Plut.

βυθιτισ.def: βυθῖτις (from βυθός) pecul. fem. of βύθιος, Anth.

βυθοσ.def: βυθός (Akin to βάθος.) the depth, esp. of the sea, the deep, Aesch., Soph.

βυκτησ.def: βύκτης (βύω) swelling, blustering, βυκτάων ἀνέμων (epic gen.) Od.

βυρσα.gloss: the skin stripped off, a hide
βυρσα.def: βύρσα (deriv. uncertain) 1. the skin stripped off, a hide, Batr., Hdt.; βύρσης ὄζειν to smell of leather, Ar.: a drum, Eur. 2. the skin of a live animal, Theocr.

βυρσαιετοσ.def: βυρσαίετος leather-eagle, nickname of Cleon the tanner, Ar.

βυρσοδεψεω.def: βυρσοδεψέω (from βυρσοδέψης) to dress or tan hides, Ar.

βυρσοπαφλαγων.def: βυρσοπαφλαγών leather-Paphlagonian, nickname of Cleon, Ar.

βυρσοτενησ.def: βυρσοτενής (τείνω) with skin stretched over it, of a drum, Eur.

βυσσινοσ.def: βύσσινος made of βύσσος, σινδών β. a fine linen bandage, used for mummy-cloths,, Hdt.; for wounds, id.; β. πέπλοι Aesch

βυσσοδομευω.def: βυσσοδομεύω (δομέω) (only in pres. part.) to build in the deep: metaph. to brood over a thing in the depth of one's soul, ponder deeply, Od.

βυσσοθεν.def: βυσσόθεν (βυσσός) from the bottom of the sea, Soph.

βυσσομετρησ.def: βυσσομέτρης (μετρέω) measuring the deeps, epith. of a fisherman, Anth.

βυσσοσ.gloss: the depth of the sea, the bottom
βυσσοσ.def: βυσσός (= βυθός) the depth of the sea, the bottom, Il., Hdt.
βύσσος (A foreign word; cf. Hebr. butz.) a fine flax, and the linen made from it, Theocr.

βυσσωμα.def: βύσσωμα (= βύσμα) of nets, which stopped the passage of a shoal of tunnies, Anth.

βυω.def: βύω to stuff, 1. c. gen. rei, to stuff full of, only in Pass., νήματος βεβυσμένος stuffed full of spun-work or yarn, Od.; τὸ στόμα ἐβέβυστο [sc. χρυσοῦ] Hdt. 2. c. dat. rei, to stop or bung up with, plug: Pass., σπογγίωι βεβυσμένος Ar. 3. absol., βεβ. τὰ ὦτα deaf, Luc.

βωλοσ.gloss: a lump of earth, a clod
βωλοσ.def: βῶλος 1. a lump of earth, a clod, Lat. gleba, Od., Soph., Xen. 2. like Lat. gleba, land, ground, soil, Mosch., Anth. 3. generally, a lump of anything, a mass, of the sun, Eur.

βωμιοσ.def: βώμιος (βωμός) 1. of an altar, Soph., Eur. 2. of a suppliant, βωμία at the altar, id.

βωμισ.def: βωμίς (Dim. of βωμός) a step, Hdt.

βωμολοχευμα.def: βωμολόχευμα (from βωμολοχεύομαι) a piece of low flattery, in pl. base flatteries, ribald jests, Ar.

βωμολοχευομαι.gloss: to use low flattery, indulge in ribaldry
βωμολοχευομαι.def: βωμολοχεύομαι Dep. to use low flattery, indulge in ribaldry, Ar., Isocr.

βωμολοχικοσ.def: βωμολοχικός (from βωμολόχος) inclined to ribaldry, Luc.

βωμολοχοσ.gloss: one that lurked about the altars for the scraps that could be got there, a half-starved beggar
βωμολοχοσ.def: βωμολόχος (λοχάω) 1. properly one that lurked about the altars for the scraps that could be got there, a half-starved beggar, Luc. 2. metaph. one who would do any dirty work to get a meal, a lick-spittle, low jester, buffoon, Ar.:—as adj., βωμολόχον τι ἐξευρεῖν to invent some ribald trick, id.; of vulgar music, id.

βωμοσ.def: βωμός (βαίνω) 1. any raised platform, a stand, Lat. suggestus, for chariots, Il.: of a statue, a base, pedestal, Od. 2. a raised place for sacrificing, an altar, Hom., Trag., etc. 3. a tomb, cairn, Anth.

βωστρεω.def: βωστρέω (βοάω) to call on, esp. to call to aid, Od., Ar.

βωτιανειρα.def: βωτιάνειρα (βόσκω, ἀνήρ) man-feeding, nurse of heroes, Il.
